channel.title: Deep dives — The Cross Section
channel.description: The standout papers, read in full

item.title: Indication of Electron Antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background
item.dc:creator: Kamiokande Collaboration et al.
item.description:
Super-Kamiokande fits 5003.0 days (Oct 2008–Mar 2026, phases SK-IV through VIII, including the Gd-loaded phases) and finds a DSNB flux of 3.6⁺¹.6_-1.5 cm⁻²s⁻¹ (4.8⁺².2_-2.0 events/yr) for E_ν>13.3 MeV, assuming the Horiuchi+09 6 MeV spectral shape. The background-only hypothesis is disfavored at 2.6σ (one-sided). The Kresse+21 and Ashida+23 shapes give 2.7σ and 2.6σ. The Gd phases alone give 2.2σ and the pure-water phases 1.4σ. The simpler model-independent count over 13.3–31.3 MeV gives only 1.8σ (p = 0.036). The best-fit flux sits at the upper end of the Horiuchi+09 range of 2.1–3.9 cm⁻²s⁻¹.

On the digest’s question of where the gain comes from: - Background rejection. An ML NC classifier raises IBD efficiency from 79% to 89% and halves the residual NCQE fraction from 10% to 5%. - Systematics. A T2K beam sample cuts the NC rate uncertainty from 70% to 45%. The neutron-multiplicity uncertainty falls from 30–40% to 10–30%, and the ⁹Li remaining-rate error from 50% to 30%. - Thresholds. The N_n=1 threshold drops from 15.5 to 11.5 MeV.

The paper says only that the combined effect more than doubles the median discovery potential. The provided text does not split that gain by component.

The key caveat is in Appendix B. With the old N_n≠1 threshold, the pure-water phases show an extra contribution at 15.5–21.5 MeV, comparable to the expected signal. Including it shifts the fitted DSNB rate by about 1σ, which is more than statistics should allow. The collaboration attributes this to mismodeled spallation and raises that threshold to 21.5 MeV, at a 13.9% cost in expected signal. That is conservative, but it also shows the spallation model is not yet under control at the sensitivity now being reached.

item.title: Observation of the T_cc̅1(4430)⁻ state in B⁰→D^*-D⁰K⁺ decays
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
LHCb’s amplitude analysis uses 6912 candidates from 9 fb⁻¹, with about 5% background. A model containing only D⁰K⁺ resonances describes the D⁰K⁺ and D^-K⁺ spectra but misses a dip near 4.4 GeV in m(D^-D⁰⁾ (χ²⁼⁸².1 over 64 Dalitz bins).

Adding the T_cc̅1(4430)⁻ with its mass and width fixed gives 2ΔNLL =-43.0, which is 6.2σ statistical and 5.3σ after systematics. The state appears through destructive interference rather than as a peak. Its own fit fraction is (1.3±0.4)%, while its interference with the QMI S-wave is (-6.6±1.3)%. J^P=1⁺ is preferred over the alternatives at more than 5σ.

Other results: - With mass and width free, the fit gives 4424±21⁺¹²_-6 MeV and 145±39±17 MeV. These sit 1.8σ and 0.7σ from the ψ(2S)π values, so “consistent” carries a mild mass pull. - Substituting the T_cc̅1(4200) gives only 3.6σ. With both states included, the 4200 drops to 1.6σ. - The T_cc̅1(3900) and T^*_c̅s̅1(2900) are not significant (fit fractions below 0.24% and 0.32% at 95% CL).

This is the first open-charm decay of the state. The measured width ratio Γ(D^*-D⁰⁾/Γ(ψ(2S)π⁻⁾⁼⁰.96±0.29⁺⁰.22_-0.48⁺⁰.57_-0.30 disfavors dominance of either channel. The authors note that theory predictions for this ratio are lacking.

The main caveat is that the dominant systematic is amplitude modeling. The overlapping D⁰K⁺ 1⁻ wave, which carries about 75% of the fit fractions, is described by splines, with a K-matrix alternative used as the systematic variation. The two diverge in phase above 3 GeV.

item.title: A Low Scale for Quark–Lepton Unification
item.dc:creator: Lawrence J. Hall et al.
item.description:
Running the Standard Model Yukawas at two loops, the authors find that y_τ=y_b holds at μ_3=5.20⁺⁰.90_-0.76×10⁵ GeV and y_μ=3y_s at μ_2=7.20⁺³.69_-2.33×10⁵ GeV. The ratio μ_2/μ_3 is stable under three-loop running (1.39 → 1.40). The Georgi–Jarlskog relation y_e=y_d/3 arrives later, at about 3×10⁸ GeV. For contrast, at 2×10¹⁶ GeV the three ratios are off by 30–70%.

A sparse Pati–Salam texture produces all three relations. An SU(4)-singlet bidoublet fills the 12, 21 and 33 entries, and an adjoint fills the 22 entry. However, tree-level vector-leptoquark exchange in K_L→μe requires M_X≳2.5×10⁶ GeV, which is above μ_2,3. That leaves two routes: - Electron mass from elsewhere. The heavier-generation relations then survive at (5–7)×10⁵ GeV, with K→μμ as the leading probe. - Two fixed-parameter theories that keep all three relations: - The “123” theory reaches unification through flavor diagonalization alone, at 4.6⁺¹.2_-0.9×10⁶ GeV. - The “12” theory has symmetric Yukawas and unifies at 1.5⁺⁰.7_-0.5×10⁷ GeV. It predicts |V_cb|=0.042±0.002; the paper compares this only to the PDG value 0.0411±0.0012. It also needs an 11% charged-scalar threshold, a negligible up-sector 2–3 rotation, and sinβ≈0.07–0.17.

The μ→e conversion rate is CR_Al≈2.8×10⁻¹⁷⁽¹⁰⁷ GeV/M_X)⁴. Mu2e and COMET Phase II reach about 8×10⁶ GeV, covering most of the 123 range; Mu2e-II and AMF would cover both theories.

Caveats: - About 75–90% of the variance in the unification scales comes from m_d and m_s. - The leading-order texture predicts |V_us|=0.219 against a measured 0.2243; matching it needs a relative phase of about 92° between the up and down light blocks. - Scalar contributions to μ→e conversion are omitted. - In G_422, nucleon-decay bounds of several 10⁶ GeV can arise, but they depend on assumed Planck-suppressed operator coefficients.

item.title: Analytic two-loop corrections to top-quark pair production at hadron colliders
item.dc:creator: Federico Buccioni et al.
item.description:
Buccioni, Nega, Sauer, Tancredi and Wagner give the complete two-loop qq̅→tt̅ and gg→tt̅ amplitudes in analytic form, with full m_t, N_c, n_l and n_h dependence, through 𝒪(ε²⁾. The 789 gg and 218 qq̅ two-loop diagrams reduce to 417 masters. These are cast into ε-factorised differential equations spanning 13 elliptic curves and one genus-two curve, which lives in the non-planar sector nB463. Up to weight four, 300 of the 449 independent differential forms enter the finite remainder. None of the quadratic-type elliptic forms survive, but 55 of the 85 genus-two forms do. That is the basis for the “first genus-two finite remainder” claim; the curve itself had been identified earlier.

Boundary values are fixed at threshold. The authors run AMFlow at (x_1,x_2)=(10⁻⁴,2·10⁻⁴⁾ with 100–300 digits, match to generalised series, then fit constants with PSLQ. The elliptic and genus-two constants resist any known basis and are kept numerically. The public hqpAmp code evaluates renormalised finite remainders across phase space, switching between double and quad precision.

On practical impact, NNLO tt̅ already ran on numerical grids, and the qq̅ channel was already analytic. The gains here are: - control and speed; - 𝒪(ε¹,2) terms for three-loop IR studies; - a stress test of canonical-basis methods beyond elliptic.

The paper does not address bound-state effects. Its threshold expansions are fixed-order input that toponium-vs-continuum fits would still need to combine with a Coulomb/NRQCD treatment.

item.title: The Galactic Center Gamma-Ray Excess and the Look-Elsewhere Effect
item.dc:creator: Isabel S. Sands et al.
item.description:
Sands and Hopkins analyse two FIRE-2 Milky Way analogs, m12f and m12m (m12i is dropped for its warped disk), with spectrally resolved CR transport. They compare each snapshot over 460–20 Myr lookback against a baseline “template”: the mean of the snapshots whose total ROI flux is below the median. For every ROI (10°, 20°) and line-of-sight cut (0, 2, 7 kpc), the Fermi GCE lies inside the 25th–75th percentile band of residuals, and many residuals are several times larger. One m12f snapshot matches the GCE in spectrum and is roughly spherical inside 10°, produced by at least three clustered supernova episodes. The physical driver is that CR diffusion across the central kpc takes ~1 Myr, comparable to the timescale of ISM disruption, so steady-state templates are structurally inadequate.

The caveats are substantial, and the authors state most of them: - Star formation. Central SFRs are 1–2 orders of magnitude above the CMZ, and total diffuse flux is a few to 10 times Fermi’s. The residual amplitude is therefore compared against a much brighter galaxy. - Sample size. There are only two galaxies and no AGN, so no frequency or look-elsewhere statistic can be computed. - Baseline choice. A baseline built from below-median snapshots biases residuals positive. - Comparison method. Residuals here are not a template fit; the authors’ proposed test is to run actual Fermi pipelines on the simulations.

A potentially useful discriminant is that the excesses are typically flanked by in-plane flux deficits.

item.title: FeynFacet: AI agents for analytic NLO QCD
item.dc:creator: Zhong-Bo Kang et al.
item.description:
Kang, Vogelsang and Zhang use LLM agents to write and run the process-specific programs for analytic NLO calculations. Physicists fix the observables, projections and HVBM conventions, and the finished programs run without further model calls. The pipeline: - spin and colour algebra done in parallel with FeynCalc, FORM and Tracer; - reverse unitarity for the real-emission phase space; - dimensional shifts to remove evanescent numerators; - Kira IBP at symbolic d, then SubTropica for the masters.

The new results are NLO transverse-spin-transfer hard functions: - all seven q^↑b→c^↑X classes through α_s³, including the regular-only q^↑g→q̅^↑X from identical-quark interference; - ℓq^↑→q^↑X through α_em²α_s, with the scattered lepton integrated.

They find σ̂_T,XX=σ̂_T,NN in every channel, so the spin dependence is purely cos(ϕ_a-ϕ_c).

Validation reproduces published UU/LL pp and ℓp results, double-transverse pp, and the one-loop TMD matching and soft functions. The checks on the new results are weaker than on the benchmarks: - The pp transfer results agree across the three algebra routes only at test points. Crossing from incoming-TT is symbolic only at Born level. - The ℓp result has no external benchmark, only Born normalisation, pole cancellation and RG checks. - All three routes share the same generated amplitudes, reduction and masters, so common-mode errors would go undetected.

As a test case for agentic theory work, the release of code alongside the coefficients is what makes it auditable.

item.title: Measurements of the branching fractions of Λ_c⁺→ΛK⁺π⁰ and Λ_c⁺→ΛK⁺η decays at Belle and Belle II
item.dc:creator: Belle et al.
item.description:
Belle and Belle II (980 + 570 fb⁻¹) report the first observation of Λ_c⁺→ΛK⁺η at >10σ statistical significance, from 1107 ± 45 signal events. Relative to the reference mode, the measured ratio is ℬ/ℬ(Λπ⁺π⁰⁾⁼⁽⁸.73±0.35±0.43)×10⁻³, giving ℬ=(6.20±0.25±0.31±0.30)×10⁻⁴. The three SU(3)_F predictions are (1.9±0.6), (0.45±0.10) and (0.59±0.24)×10⁻⁴. The measurement exceeds them by 5.5σ, 11.2σ and 10.1σ respectively. The companion SCS mode is measured as ℬ(ΛK⁺π⁰⁾⁼⁽¹.29±0.05±0.05±0.06)×10⁻³. This agrees with BESIII and with the 2024 fit that includes the color-symmetric Hamiltonian (1.36 ± 0.25), and sits well below the earlier 3.5–4.5 × 10⁻³ predictions. The precision is markedly improved over BESIII’s ±0.27 statistical error.

So the same SU(3)_F fit that now gets ΛK⁺π⁰ right undershoots ΛK⁺η by an order of magnitude. That is the charm-baryon entry in the season’s flavor-symmetry strain noted in the digest. The caveat is visible in the paper itself. The two-body invariant-mass spectra deviate significantly from phase space, and efficiencies are reweighted to the data Dalitz distribution. The predictions assume non-resonant, S-wave-dominated meson pairs, so intermediate resonances in ΛK⁺η (smaller phase space) could account for the excess rather than a failure of the symmetry itself. A Dalitz analysis would discriminate. On the experimental side, the η systematic is dominated by photon reconstruction (4.4%), and there is a 4.8% reference-BF uncertainty.

item.title: Faithful Uncertainties in ML-Based Inverse Problems: GPs, NNs and NTKs for the Triplet PDF
item.dc:creator: Nina Elmer et al.
item.description:
Methods that agree on the central T_3 disagree on what their error bars mean. The setup is a closure test on BCDMS F_2^p-F_2^d, using 248 points with the full covariance, NNPDF4.0 truth, and a data region of x≳0.07. The normalised bias R_b is computed on a single L_1 realisation:

Model R_b (full covariance) R_b (diagonal only)
RBF GP 1.08 0.38
Gibbs GP 0.86 0.53
NTK, trained 0.67 —
NTK, at initialisation 9.5 —
L_2 NN ensemble 0.74 —
L_1 NN ensemble 2.84 —

The L_1 ensemble excludes data uncertainty by construction, so its large value is expected. Dropping covariance correlations shifts R_b non-monotonically, so pointwise width alone does not determine calibration. Two other failure modes stand out: - Heteroscedastic loss. It learns broad diagonal variances, which the authors read as likelihood misspecification rather than faithful uncertainty. - Endpoint preprocessing. It sets the small-x answer. The fit at α=1 versus α=0.5 is identical in the data region but diverges below 0.07. Preprocessed GP variance vanishes at the endpoints by construction, giving bands that miss the truth.

In the HERA extrapolation test, the initialisation NTK degrades NC-EM by Δn_σ≈5.0, while all other models stay below 1. The authors are candid about the limits. With n_eig = 4–19, the test rules out gross underestimates but cannot certify faithfulness. A single seed visibly changes the reconstructions, and the L_2 ensemble is only NNPDF-inspired.

item.title: Same Events, Weaker Bound: Model Dependence in Magellanic Microlensing Limits on Primordial Black Holes
item.dc:creator: David Morales-Zapien et al.
item.description:
The authors hold OGLE’s 13 events, efficiencies and t_E posteriors fixed and change only the rate model, inside OGLE’s own relaxed likelihood. The benchmark uses a flattened MW halo (q_h=0.72, ρ_⊙=0.30 GeV cm⁻³), a cored Burkert LMC halo, Ibata disks, and a lighter LMC with a shallower IMF. It weakens the 20-year relaxed limit by up to 1.6 near 0.32 M_⊙. A deliberately extreme stress test weakens it by up to 3.4.

The headline “~6×” (6.2 for the benchmark, 13.2 for the stress test) is relative to the strict limit, so it also folds in OGLE’s own event-origin difference. In the planetary-mass window, the factors are 1.19 and 2.39 for smooth PBHs, and 3.4 and 6.0 for 30 pc clusters under a Lyα shot-noise cap. A one-at-a-time ablation at 0.45 M_⊙ shows the IMF matters most (R=0.68), while the heavier disks push the other way (1.10). LMC-induced disequilibrium raises the lensing-weighted halo density by about 6%, undercutting a common critique.

The caveats are explicit: - Parameters were chosen to suppress the rate and are fixed, not marginalized. - The IMF endpoints are not a joint confidence region. - The stress test conflicts with 6D tracer masses. - Its isothermal LMC halo fails the LMC mass constraints.

Oddly, the weaker limits coexist with a larger preference for nonzero f near 0.03 M_⊙: Δχ²⁼⁹.2–10.2, versus 3.7 in OGLE’s analysis.

item.title: The renormalization-group running of neutrino mixing is undetectable
item.dc:creator: Gabriela Barenboim et al.
item.description:
Barenboim, Bustamante and Liu argue that every experiment measures one physical mixing matrix Û. They define it by the eigenvectors of the on-shell physical mass matrix m_eff=m(μ)+Σ_M-12(Σ_K^Tm+mΣ_K), which does not depend on μ. Momentum transfer Q never flows through the external-leg self-energy. If one sets μ=Q, that self-energy picks up ln(Q²/M_X²⁾ terms that rotate U(Q) back to Û. The premise in the prior literature keeps U(Q) but drops these logs, which the authors call an inconsistent truncation.

Only vertex and box corrections carry both flavor and Q dependence, and they lack the 1/(m_i-m_j) degeneracy enhancement. The paper gives their sizes in each setting: - MSSM: a flavor-diagonal ~0.7% rescaling of the ν_τ coupling at 10 TeV. - GeV HNL: at most 4×10⁻⁹. - Light-scalar seesaw: zero at one loop.

For Model 2 of Babu et al., the claimed running disappears once the Dirac masses are allowed to run along with Y_N.

Independently of the theory argument, NuTeV and NOMAD limits on zero-baseline transitions would require |Δθ_23|<0.7^∘, |Δθ_12|<2.3^∘, |Δθ_13|<2.4^∘ and |Δδ_CP|<16^∘ between m_π and a few GeV, if the premise held. This bound excludes the β_δ=0.15 used to illustrate a proposed reactor signal.

Caveats: - The data bounds assume one parameter shifts at a time, so correlated shifts could partly compensate. - They do not apply when running starts above a few GeV, as in the MSSM case or the ~5 GeV double-bang configuration. There only the theory argument applies. - Off-diagonal vertex terms beyond the SM, up to ~10⁻², survive and act as non-standard charged-current interactions. - Two of the targeted papers are the authors’ own, including a step-at-Q=M HNL paper they now say also used an incorrect δm. That self-correction gives the refutation more weight.

item.title: Simulation-Informed High-Velocity Dark Matter in the Effective Theory of Direct Detection
item.dc:creator: Xiuyuan Zhang et al.
item.description:
Zhang, Herrera, Thoyas and Necib build a local dark matter (DM) velocity distribution from two pieces: - a Gaia DR3 reconstruction, combining Gaia–Sausage–Enceladus stars convolved with a simulation-calibrated kernel and a generalized-Gaussian diffuse component; - the m12b LMC analog from FIRE-2, which contributes 32 particles at 738–846 km/s and 0.3% of the local density.

The resulting laboratory-frame endpoints, and the maximum accessible splitting δ_max for a 1 TeV particle on xenon, are:

Distribution Endpoint (km/s) δ_max (keV)
Standard Halo Model (SHM) 793 381
Reconstruction alone 835 423
Reconstruction + LMC 846 434
Auriga-25 (Au-25) 975 575

Limits across all 14 non-relativistic EFT operators coincide below δ≈200 keV and then fan out. Velocity-suppressed operators separate first.

For 𝒪_1, the region that fits the LZ 248 keV event plus empty sidebands sits at different splittings: - SHM: δ=304–360 keV. - FIRE-based: 320–390 keV. - Au-25: 376–448 keV, with mass confined to 171–468 GeV.

In the digest’s context, a tail reaching 1100 km/s would need support well beyond anything here.

The authors are explicit that the result is limited: - The tail rests on 32 particles. - The Sun has to be placed out of the disk to match the LMC geometry. With the observer in the disk, the LMC particles come out slower. - The Milky Way-only endpoint has a 16–84% posterior spread of 773–912 km/s. - Their counting likelihood differs from LZ’s published limits by up to ~3×. - They conclude that a single LMC analog cannot define the tail uniquely.

item.title: Radiative corrections to double-β decay and their impact on experimental analyses
item.dc:creator: Jordy de Vries et al.
item.description:
This is the full companion to the authors’ earlier Letter. In a heavy-nucleus EFT with explicit 1⁺ intermediate states, de Vries, Mereghetti, el Morabit and Sandner compute all 𝒪(α) virtual and real corrections for arbitrary excitation energy ω_n. They also give new closed-form heavy-propagator triangle and box integrals via an auxiliary-mass trick.

Main structural results: - No Z-enhanced terms survive. The 𝒪(αZ) and 𝒪(αZ²⁾ terms cancel class by class, except the static Coulomb piece already contained in the Fermi functions. - A new topology matters. The electron–electron box has no single-β analogue and brings in dependence on the two-electron invariant mass s. - The correction factorizes at large ω_n. At leading order in 1/ω_n it is the tree-level rate times a “double-weak Sirlin function” f_2ν(β_1,β_2,β_12). This function differs from the sum of two single-β Sirlin functions, and its μ dependence cancels against g_V⁴ (g_V-1≈1.9–2.0% at μ=2E_0). - One new nuclear input appears at next order. It is ζ_31, a log-weighted M_GT ratio, which the authors find negligible. - There is a non-trivial check. The total-visible-energy spectrum has no lnm_e dependence as m_e→0, as the Kinoshita–Lee–Nauenberg theorem requires.

Because the electron-only and calorimetric (ϵ_tot) spectra differ, the correction depends on how a detector handles the real photon. The authors provide the fully differential photon spectrum and ask experiments to simulate it. For 0νββ, the inclusive rate rises by ~5%, independent of the nuclear matrix elements and m_ββ.

The extracted text ends before the numerical ξ_31-bias results, so their size cannot be quoted here.

Acknowledged approximations: - 𝒪(αZRE_e) finite-size terms are not yet mapped rigorously. - The Fermi function F is also used for the β_1β_2y_12 term. - The 1/ω_n expansion holds for ¹³⁶Xe, but the authors cite larger deviations for ⁸²Se.

item.title: : The Electron-Recoil Response Tail and the LZ High-Energy Event Background
item.description:
The published LZ response does not fix the ER leakage that the 248 keV event’s background estimate depends on. The authors rebuild the ER continuum from NEST’s EFT2024 configuration and get a per-decay leakage of P≃1.3×10⁻⁷ at a 4.1σ displacement in N_e. That yields N^ER_leak=(1.9±0.1±0.4)×10⁻⁴ counts, against LZ’s 0.0106 total in the 500<S1c<600 phd region. They then construct three families of distributions (generalised-normal, skew-t, Johnson S_U) that match the executable model’s mean, variance and skewness exactly. The families agree within a factor of ~2 at matched quantile deviation, yet the tail probability spans more than five orders of magnitude.

The thresholds are close to the model:

  • 0.14% quantile agreement: ER reaches 10% of the quoted background.
  • 0.47%: ER equals the whole quoted background.
  • 1.10%: ER reaches 0.1 counts.

LZ’s counter-argument, that no events appear between the event and the ER band, does not discriminate between these tails. Even the heaviest family predicts only 0.69 events in that gap. Two further points:

  • Printed vs. implemented response. The printed Supplement Eq. 4 gives a fluctuation width 1.475× the implemented one. Taken literally, it implies 0.60 ER counts, far above LZ’s quoted total for all backgrounds.
  • Calibration reach. The tritium and ¹⁴C calibrations stop at S1c = 500 phd, while the event sits at 540 phd.

Caveats. The authors explicitly do not claim the tail is wrong, and they do not propagate the result to LZ’s 2.6σ global (3.4σ local) significance. The link between the NEST commit and the Letter is circumstantial. The ER selection efficiency is unpublished. The ¹²⁴Xe/¹²⁵I lines are excluded.

What would settle it. A tail measurement at the 10⁻⁵ level near N_q∼5×10³, or a shape fit using ~3×10³ events per slice (rising to 3×10⁴ for the mildest problematic tail).

item.title: : Isospin breaking in ρππ couplings
item.description:
The missing isospin-breaking (IB) ρππ coupling correction comes out small and cuts the corresponding τ-route uncertainty to roughly a third of the White Paper’s assumed ±4.7×10⁻¹⁰. The method is a symmetry-preserving Dyson–Schwinger/Bethe–Salpeter contact-interaction model. IB enters dynamically through flavour-dependent beyond-rainbow-ladder couplings ξ_u,d, tuned to Δm_ρ, and explicitly through m_d/m_u∈[1,2]. Results:

  • Coupling ratio: g_ρ⁰ππ/g_ρ⁺ππ=1.0024(17)(1).
  • Width difference: ΔΓ_ρ=+0.39(51) MeV, compatible with but tighter than PDG (+0.31 ± 1.3) and a data-based extraction (−0.58 ± 1.01).
  • Effect on a_μ: the ρππ term is Δa_μ=-2.32(1.64)×10⁻¹⁰, about one-third of the White Paper’s error.

The −2.32 is not the net shift. It nearly cancels against the radiative-correction term (−2.22) and the pion-mass phase-space term (+4.09). The total form-factor-ratio IB is -0.25(1.64)×10⁻¹⁰, compared with the older -1.62(65)×10⁻¹⁰.

Caveats. - The contact interaction is a crude kernel; the symmetric coupling comes out at 6.29 against 5.94 from the PDG width. - The error is driven almost entirely by the poorly known input Δm_ρ=0.7(0.8) MeV. - The τ-side numbers rely on a Gounaris–Sakurai parametrisation. - The same framework predicts R_ϕ=1.484±0.029, 2.2σ below BESIII.

item.title: : Automation of amplitude-level QED resummation with ACRAIC
item.description:
The extracted text cuts off before the validation section, so the headline numbers here come from the abstract.

ACRAIC brings coherent (CEEX-style) amplitude-level YFS exponentiation to general processes inside Sherpa. Previously this existed only for hand-coded fermion-pair production in KKMC. The generalisation works in three steps:

  • Photon assignment. The initial/final assignment of photons becomes an assignment to emission stages. Gauge invariance forces these stages to be partitions of the charged legs into charge-neutral sets, including resonance stages for Z/γ^* and W pairs.
  • Remainders. The infrared-finite remainders are tree-level helicity amplitudes with N+2 and N+3 legs and partition-dependent propagator shifts, computed by Comix’s Berends–Giele recursion.
  • Virtual correction. The one-loop electroweak virtual enters as a per-helicity factor from OpenLoops or Recola.

Validation is against KKMC for e⁺e⁻→μ⁺μ⁻ at photonic 𝒪(α²⁾. Comparison is also made with the squared-level YFS_NLO_EW, which shares the resummation and differs only in matching. At 𝒪(α²⁾ the two matchings agree on the size of the missing higher orders to ~10⁻³, and the perturbative uncertainty drops about tenfold relative to 𝒪(α). The author reports that squared-level matching can go unstable in four-lepton production while the amplitude-level version stays stable. Example applications are the FCC-ee Higgs recoil mass and Z-pole distributions.

Caveats. - “Photonic 𝒪(α²⁾” omits two-loop γZ boxes and weak corrections. - The paper is described as mostly technical, with phenomenology left to dedicated studies.

item.title: First observation of weak magnetism in neutron decay
item.dc:creator: Miriam Camarasa-Domene et al.
item.description:
The weak-magnetism form factor comes out as g_M = 4.47(87), which excludes g_M=0 at 5.1σ and sits 0.3σ from the CVC value of 4.71. The β asymmetry alone cannot separate g_M from λ. The authors fix λ= -1.27598(61) independently, using r_nτ_n(1+3λ²⁾⁼²ℱt with: - τ_n=878.36(43) s, the PDG bottle average with S=1.81; - ℱt=3070.01(1.90) s from ²⁶mAl alone, reanalyzed with updated charge radii.

They then reinterpret the asymmetry data as an effective Ã that carries explicit g_M dependence. Two refinements matter: - They evaluate the energy moments over each experiment’s actual window rather than the full phase space. This raises the g_M sensitivity relative to the earlier 3σ global fit. - The linearized version, g_M = 4.40(50)_ℱt(39)_τ_n(59)_Ã, shows that all three inputs contribute comparably to the error.

The robustness checks are the main content. The significance ranges across dataset choices as follows:

Dataset choice g_M Significance
Lifetime set including beam values (S=2.3) 4.63(92) 5.0σ
Adding the a, B, λ_AB correlations 4.85(85) 5.7σ
PERKEO III + UCNτ only 4.68(81) 5.8σ
Post-2012 asymmetries only (no scale factor needed) 5.00(82) 6.1σ

Fitting the spectral shape of A(E_e) would tighten σ(g_M) by only 3–7%, based on Asimov studies. A recast of the PERKEO III Fierz likelihood gives a consistent 5.07(92).

Caveats: - The baseline ℱt rests on a single transition. It carries a δ_NS error (1.44 s) that is comparable to its statistical error. - The λ determination relies on the SM relation between τ_n and ℱt. The result is therefore a consistency test within the SM, not a model-independent extraction.

item.title: Measurement of the neutrino cross section across the TeV scale using IceCube data
item.dc:creator: Rasmi Hajjar et al.
item.description:
The analysis uses only the public eight-year IceCube upgoing-track sample: 305,735 events, more than 99.9% pure ν_μ CC. It extracts the average ν/ν̄ CC cross section in five bins from 150 GeV to 40 TeV. Earth absorption and the event energy distribution break the flux–cross-section degeneracy. Relative to CSMS, the normalizations are:

Bin Normalization
0.15–0.36 TeV 1.11⁺⁰.12_-0.13
0.36–1.17 TeV 1.22⁺⁰.24_-0.17
1.17–3.79 TeV 1.11⁺⁰.15_-0.12
3.79–12.3 TeV 0.92⁺⁰.15_-0.12
12.3–40 TeV 1.01⁺⁰.15_-0.13

All bins are within 20% and consistent with the SM. This bridges the energy-resolved collider points (up to about 2 TeV) and the astrophysical ones (above about 10 TeV). Between 360 GeV and 2 TeV the uncertainties already beat FASER’s.

Freeing ν and ν̄ separately gives a non-zero ν̄ cross section above 360 GeV at only 1.6σ (p = 0.06). That drops to 1.1σ if σ_ν>σ_ν̅ is enforced, because it is partly driven by an anticorrelated swap in bin 4 (ν: 0.40, ν̄: 2.1).

The main caveat for anyone treating this as a reference curve is the first bin. It carries a 16% Gaussian prior from fixed-target data, and that prior anchors the atmospheric flux normalization. Without it: - the fit prefers a lower flux; - the other four bins shift up by 20–30%; - the first bin lands about 2σ above CSMS.

So the result is limited by the flux–cross-section anticorrelation and is partly calibrated by accelerator input. A tenfold exposure forecast gives under 10% on the average cross section and more than 7σ for ν̄.

item.title: Dark Matter Interpretations of the Galactic Center Gamma-Ray Excess with 18 Years of Fermi-LAT Data and the FL16Y Source Catalog
item.dc:creator: Sang Hwan Kim et al.
item.description:
The GCE is re-extracted from 17.7 years of FRONT-only data with FL16Y masks, scanning 80 GALPROP diffuse models. Model X fits best, ahead of the next model by Δ(-2lnℒ)=72. Systematics come from a full 14×14 covariance built from 22 Galactic-plane control regions.

Against new combined limits from 30 dwarfs, with J-factor uncertainties profiled, the picture is: - bb̅ and other hadronic channels: the best fit is (39.5 GeV, 1.2×10⁻²⁶ cm³/s) with χ² = 27.5/12. Its entire 68% region lies above the dSph limit, as do those for cc̅, light quarks and gluons. - Effective four-body channels: the 68% regions for 4b and 2b2τ are fully excluded. - τ⁺τ⁻: the best fit (9.3 GeV, χ² = 22.8/12) sits just 0.67% above the limit, and part of its 68% region survives. - 4τ: the best fit is 8.7% above the limit, and part of its 68% region survives. - 4b cascades: these fit best near r=m_ϕ/m_χ≃0.3. Per the abstract, part of the 68% region stays below the limits for r≲0.4.

AMS-02 antiprotons are generally weaker than the dwarfs and constrain only part of the 4b cascade region. That antiproton likelihood uses the BIG propagation model and includes only the experimental covariance; adding propagation-model uncertainties could weaken it further.

For GCE model-building, including today’s dark-Higgs construction, this leaves a τ-rich or light-mediator corridor.

Caveats are substantial: - The exclusions are conditional on Model X and a fixed γ = 1.2 gNFW J-factor. - The 80-model envelope, a factor 3–4 above 1 GeV, is shown but not propagated. - Even the best fits have χ²/dof ≈ 2. - Extending the dwarf data from 14.3 to 17.7 years weakens the high-mass limits for every catalog tested, and the authors do not yet understand why.

item.title: Complete g⁶ pressure of hot Yang–Mills theory
item.dc:creator: Keijo Kajantie et al.
item.description:
The missing nonlogarithmic hard coefficient is β̃_E1=6236±40. That converts to q_c(N_c=3,N_f=0)=-3591.2±16.9_pert±250_mag, consistent with the old lattice-inferred β̃_E1≃6000±600.

Method. - The 65 four-loop vacuum graphs give about 10⁵ sum-integrals. These reduce to 21 canonical structures, and ξ-dependence cancels at that stage. - Nine nonfactorizing sum-integrals were unknown. The authors evaluated them with thermal loop-tree duality. Matsubara sums are done analytically, and new local IR counterterms for zero-mode soft regions are added to BPHZ-style UV subtractions. The finite remainders were Monte Carlo integrated, at roughly 10⁶ CPU-hours. - The pole coefficients come out analytically. They confirm the previously inferred hard-scale IR poles and their explicit cancellation against EQCD/MQCD. - The method independently reproduces the known I_6.

Lattice comparison. The comparison uses Borsanyi et al. data in an EQCD-resummed scheme, with scale set by FAC and varied by a factor of 2. The band agrees with the data down to a few T_c. In the same scheme, g³ and g⁴ overshoot Stefan–Boltzmann and g⁵ undershoots. The authors read this as support for the “Laine conjecture”.

Caveats. - The magnetic constant B_G now dominates the error, by a factor of about 15 over the new perturbative piece. - The full result holds only for SU(3), because the four-loop MQCD matching is incomplete for general N_c. - The “only at g⁶” statement is tied to this resummation prescription. The authors note that other schemes behave better at lower orders.

item.title: The pressure of the gluon plasma at 𝒪(g_s⁶⁾, perturbatively
item.dc:creator: Mikael Chala et al.
item.description:
This is an independent route to the same quantity, giving q_c(0)=-3846±515. That is about 0.5σ from the value -3526(4)(55)(30) obtained by fitting the g⁶ formula to Borsanyi et al. trace-anomaly data over 10–1000 Λ_MS.

Method. - Background-field Feynman gauge, with a different propagator basis. - Reduction via SIRENA using unimodular loop-momentum changes and no genuine four-loop IBP. This yields 10 connected and 6 factorizable sum-integrals. - The connected integrals are evaluated numerically: Schwinger parameters, sector/subsector decomposition, partial Poisson resummation, and Sobol QMC with 4 Matsubara modes. - Poles are cross-checked by doing the hard-to-soft matching in the full bosonic SM 3D EFT. This needs a four-loop EFT vacuum counterterm that they compute for the first time. The resulting 22 equations have rank 14 and fix 7 pole combinations.

Lattice comparison. The strict expansion at μ̅=2πT matches the lattice within 3% above 2.5 Λ_MS, and within 1.5% from 3 to 1000 Λ_MS.

Caveats. - The error is about twice the Helsinki total. The two β_G errors alone account for only about ±170 of it, so the numerical sum-integral allowances dominate. - Both groups compare against the same lattice dataset, so the lattice check is not independent across the two papers. - The cross-check between the groups covers one shared master integral and the final q_c; the two central values differ by about 255.

item.title: Explaining b→sℓ⁺ℓ⁻ with CKM Unitarity Violation? A No-Go Theorem
item.dc:creator: Andreas Crivellin et al.
item.description:
Updated fit. The authors refit LFU b→sℓℓ data with new LHCb/CMS inputs. The best fit is C_9=-0.87, C_10=0.24, at 5.4σ (Δχ²≈33). This excludes the bins nearest the J/ψ.

The proposed escape. Rescaling V_cb, and hence V_ts, alone can buy about 23 units of χ². The natural operator for this is C⁽³⁾_23 (for C⁽³⁾_22, the required couplings are 𝒪(10)). But SMEFT/WET running gives C_9≈(33C⁽³⁾_23+24C⁽¹⁾_23) and C_10≈-20(30C⁽³⁾_23+27C⁽¹⁾_23), in units of TeV/Λ² at Λ=2 TeV. So custodial C⁽¹⁾⁼⁻C⁽³⁾ at the high scale does not survive.

Why it fails. - Requiring the right-sign δV_cb together with C_9<0 forces C_10≲-22C_9. - The only good-fit region is fine-tuned: C⁽¹⁾_23≈-1.1C⁽³⁾_23, C⁽³⁾_23≈-1. There the V_cb shift has the wrong sign and is overcompensated by Z-b-s. - A 10% positive shift already raises the B_s-mixing prediction by about 20%. - Vector-like quarks at 2 TeV, either U alone or the custodial pairs D+T_2 and T_1+T_2, cap C_9 below a quarter of the needed size, given B_s mixing, EWPO and ϵ_K.

Scope caveats. - Right-handed currents (O_Hud) are excluded. The authors argue these cannot resolve the inclusive/exclusive V_cb split. - The analysis fixes the scale at 2 TeV. - The underlying anomaly still rests on form-factor and nonlocal-hadronic inputs.

item.title: Determining the Threshold Excess in Top-Quark Pair Production through a Global PDF Analysis
item.dc:creator: Richard D. Ball et al.
item.description:
The fit. Ball and ter Hoeve float a threshold excess Δ alongside m_t, α_s(m_Z) and the PDFs. They use the Theory Covariance Method on ATLAS and CMS m_tt̅-differential data, measured against fixed-order NNLO QCD with NLO EW and missing-higher-order uncertainties. The Δ prior is deliberately broad, at 200% of a 6.43 pb (13 TeV) / 2.19 pb (8 TeV) central value.

Results. - 13 TeV: Δ= 14.14⁺⁶.44_-6.31 pb and m_t = 172.85⁺⁰.59_-0.58 GeV, which is 2.2σ from the continuum. The m_t error is 2.3× larger than in their Δ-free fit, and the correlation is ρ(Δ,m_t)=0.84. - 8 TeV: Δ= 0.57±3.83 pb, or 3.28⁺².66_-2.32 pb with positivity imposed, with ρ=0.69. They attribute the energy dependence to the gluon being probed at higher x at 8 TeV. - Conditioned on m_t=172.5 GeV: Δ= 11.14⁺⁴.08_-4.41 pb. This is close to the ATLAS (9.3 pb) and CMS (8.8 pb) toponium cross sections but with larger errors, which the authors suggest come from the PDF correlation.

Why it matters. Any threshold-excess number is effectively a statement about m_t as well. Conversely, m_t fits that ignore Δ absorb part of the excess.

Caveats. - No individual 13 TeV dataset deviates significantly except CMS dilepton, at about 2σ. The excess only appears in the combination, whose central value exceeds every individual one; the authors explain this as a BLUE-type correlated-combination effect. - The 68% intervals use only replicas with Δ > 0. - Bin migrations from the top width are neglected. - The ATLAS 13 TeV inputs use 36 fb⁻¹. - Δ is defined relative to fixed-order NNLO, not NRQCD.

The proposed way to break the Δ–m_t degeneracy is to add spin-correlation observables to the fit.

item.title: Testing the inelastic dark matter interpretation of the LZ event with heavy-element experiments
item.dc:creator: Peter W. Graham et al.
item.description:
The halo question. For the 1.1 TeV thermal Higgsino, the 248 keV event’s preferred splitting depends on the halo model, but stays below the solar-capture bound (δ ≲ 566 keV) in the standard ones:

Halo model Efficiency window Preferred δ (keV) Status
SHM LZ ROI (0–250 keV) 340–360 Excluded by solar bound
Simulated LMC LZ ROI 495–515 Excluded by solar bound
SHM / LMC Full 0–650 keV Contours drop below the Higgsino line Disfavoured
LMC tail cut 100× (w=0.0026%) Full 440–510 Moves up to the Higgsino line, still excluded
LMC tail extended to v_max=1100 km/s at 10% flux Full 500–600 Partly survives

Two numbers frame the last two rows: - The 100× flux reduction corresponds to w=0.0026%, two orders of magnitude below the usual benchmarks. - The 10% flux of the extended tail sits an order of magnitude below the lowest flux current simulations resolve.

The authors’ conclusion is that the Higgsino question becomes a halo-simulation-resolution question.

Proposed tests. - Pb paleodetectors (Laurionite, 60 cm³, 15 nm SAXs): cover most of the event contour. - Two different elements: fix m_χ and δ through the apex recoil energy. - Mineral-age scans: the signal-to-noise should peak at 50–100 Myr if the tail comes from the LMC. - JUNO with a (20 m)³ Pb or ²³⁸U shell: covers the 566–600 keV window, and measures δ directly from the photon line. Varying the shell yields the decay length, which is calculable for the Higgsino.

Caveats. - The analysis rests on a single event. - The contours are relative likelihoods, not goodness of fit. - The efficiency is assumed to stay near 1 up to 650 keV, beyond LZ’s conservative ROI. - The extended tail is admittedly speculative.

item.title: Gallium Anomaly and Solar Neutrinos
item.dc:creator: Steven R. Elliott et al.
item.description:
The calibration. Elliott and Robertson use the Sun as a calibrated source. Its strength is fixed by Borexino elastic-scattering fluxes (⁷Be, CNO), the SNO neutral-current ⁸B flux, and a luminosity-constrained pp flux of 5.966(27)×10¹⁰ cm⁻²s⁻¹. Survival probabilities use JUNO and Daya Bay mixing, and solar models enter only through the MSW density profile.

Result. The predicted rate is 67.5⁺¹.4_-1.1 SNU against a measured 66.1±3.1 SNU from SAGE and Gallex/GNO, a ratio of 0.980⁺⁰.050_-0.049. The radioactive-source experiments give 0.817⁺⁰.028_-0.048. More than 90% of the solar rate comes from the ground-state cross section derived via detailed balance.

Why it matters. This disfavours the proposed ~20% factorization breakdown (Cadeddu et al.), which sits roughly 3.5σ from the solar ratio, and any error in the ⁷¹Ga cross section more generally. It also validates the extraction and counting efficiencies of SAGE, Gallex and BEST.

Correction to the digest’s framing. This removes the mundane explanations, not the anomaly. The authors conclude that its “source evidently lies elsewhere” and say nothing against sterile neutrinos.

Caveat. The solar rate is dominated by pp neutrinos (40 of 67.5 SNU). The test therefore weights the cross section differently from the source experiments.

Full text was not supplied for arXiv:2610.22224 or arXiv:2610.20793, so they are not covered here.

item.title: A global analysis of B̅→DP and B̅→D̅P decays
item.dc:creator: Bhubanjyoti Bhattacharya et al.
item.description:
Adding D⁰–D̅⁰ interference observables pushes the SU(3)_F-breaking requirement from ~20% to ~60%. The SU(3)_F-limit fit to all 25 observables (15 branching ratios, 6 direct and 4 time-dependent CP asymmetries, with β, β_s, γ fixed to world averages) gives χ²_min/dof=153.4/12. The branching ratios alone are already bad: B̅→DP gives 105/5. Splitting by strangeness, the ΔS=0 fit is excellent (0.2/1), but |T_1/T_0|-1=0.15±0.03 and |C_1/C_0|-1=0.36±0.13.

Allowing first-order breaking diagrams but capping their ratios at 30% leaves χ²_min=17.0, and every ratio saturates the cap. The dominant pulls come from 𝒜_CP(B⁻→D_CPπ⁻⁾ (χ²⁼¹⁰.3) and S(B̅⁰→D⁻π⁺⁾. Raising the cap to 60% brings χ²_min down to 2.8. The remainder is irreducible: - ~1.0 from an isospin-related pair of branching ratios; - ~1.4 from the measured S(D^±π^∓) central values exceeding the bound 2κ/(1+κ²⁾⁼⁰.0341 that their own branching ratios imply.

Alongside the ~1000% needed in B→PP, this is a second system where the symmetry expansion is under strain.

Caveats: - The 30% and 60% fits use 35 parameters for 25 observables, so there are no degrees of freedom. The case for >30% breaking rests on cap saturation and the χ²-vs-R scan. - Many fitted ratios are poorly determined (e.g. r_T_1=0.6±0.5). - The B̅→D̅P sector has only five measured branching ratios. - Isospin breaking is ignored.

item.title: Measuring V_cb at electron-proton colliders
item.dc:creator: David Marzocca
item.description:
The projection is a sub-percent |V_cb| from b-tagged charged-current DIS. The fit uses binwise ratios of b-tagged to flavour-inclusive CC counts in (x,y). It profiles projected PDFs, the other CKM elements, top background and tag calibration, with no |V_cb| prior or unitarity input. Projected precision:

Collider Luminosity Unpolarised Polarised
LHeC 1 ab⁻¹ 0.89% 0.79% (P_e=-0.8)
FCC-eh 2 ab⁻¹ — 0.67%
EIC — — 22–32%

At the EIC, |V_cb|=0 remains allowed within 3σ. For comparison, the PDG gives |V_cb|_excl=39.5±0.5 and |V_cb|_incl=42.0±0.5 (×10⁻³), so the LHeC number would be competitive with orthogonal systematics.

Calibration, not statistics, sets the floor. At the LHeC the error grows from 0.27% (statistics only) to 0.49% with CKM, PDF and top uncertainties, then to 0.79% once tag calibration is added. The b-efficiency calibration enters as roughly δ_b/2; its correlation with μ_cb is −64%. Halving calibration widths gives 0.60%, and a better tagger on top gives 0.55% at the LHeC and 0.40% at FCC-eh. Using today’s PDF4LHC21 instead of projected PDFs degrades the LHeC result to 1.0%. Mistag-shape uncertainties of 5% and 10% give 0.91% and 1.0%.

Caveats: - The calculation is Born-level with flat tag responses. - Radiative b production and photoproduction are not treated. - The neutral-current background is only modelled via an assumed electron-loss probability.

item.title: Direct Detection of Solar Neutrinos to Probe Tensions and Break Degeneracies in Long-Baseline Neutrino Experiments
item.dc:creator: Dorian W. P. Amaral et al.
item.description:
For nucleon-only NSI, current LZ and XENONnT ⁸B CEνNS data already exclude part of the complex-ℰ_eτ region that resolves the NOvA–T2K tension (|ℰ|∼0.2, ϕ∼3π/2). They do not yet reach the ℰ_eμ region.

A 200 t·yr xenon detector (XLZD or PandaX-xT) with a 1 keV_nr threshold and 6% ⁸B flux uncertainty would nearly cover the ℰ_eτ 1σ region. For electron-only couplings, LZ’s ER data are not yet sensitive.

The degeneracy argument is structural. Oscillations see only differences of diagonal couplings, while scattering sees absolute couplings. Even after profiling over ℰ_μμ, current NR (and, for electron-only couplings, LZ ER) limits cut into DUNE’s degenerate (|ℰ_eτ|,ℰ_ee-ℰ_μμ) region. They do not reach the ℰ_ττ-ℰ_μμ region.

Caveats: - Results depend strongly on the assumed (η,φ) coupling configuration. - The NR analyses assume no background, with the 12% ⁸B flux uncertainty dominant. - XENONnT ER data are excluded because its pp flux, (10.2±2.0)×10¹⁰ cm⁻²s⁻¹, sits 2.6σ from Borexino. The NSI region it prefers is largely excluded by LZ.

Full texts for arXiv:2610.19066 and arXiv:2610.20449 were not supplied, so no deep dive is given for those picks.

item.title: Planck-Scale Constraints on Quantum Gravity-Induced Neutrino Decoherence with IceCube
item.dc:creator: R. Abbasi et al.
item.description:
IceCube sees no oscillation damping in 368,071 up-going ν_μ events (10.7 yr, E_reco 0.5–100 TeV). The sample is the same as the sterile-neutrino analysis, now at 99.9% purity and split into starting and throughgoing tracks. The decoherence fits use a Lindblad operator with a single rate Γ(E)=Γ_0(E/1 TeV)ⁿ, tested in two forms: “state selection” (all eight off-identity entries Γ) and “phase perturbation.” The 90% CL limits at E_0=1 TeV are Γ_0<2.4×10⁻¹⁵, 4.6×10⁻¹⁶, 7.3×10⁻¹⁹ and 6.1×10⁻²¹ eV for n=0–3. Against the 2024 IceCube result (quoted at E_0=1 GeV), the gains are about 13× at n=2 and about 30× at n=3. At n=3 the limit falls below the natural expectation Γ_0=E_0ⁿ/M_Plⁿ⁻¹ for the first time, so a cubic-scaling effect would need extra suppression or a non-power-law form. The n=2 case matters most for theory, because it is the scaling found in string-motivated black-hole and D-foam calculations.

Caveats: - n=3 margin. Evaluating the paper’s formula at E_0=1 GeV gives about 6.7×10⁻³⁰ eV for the natural expectation, against a limit of 6.05×10⁻³⁰. That is a marginal crossing, not a deep exclusion. - n=0. The new limit is actually looser than 2024 (2.36 vs 1.17×10⁻¹⁵ eV). - Model assumptions. CPT conservation is assumed, since IceCube cannot separate ν from ν̅. The D matrix is diagonal, and decoherence is taken as independent of matter density. - Fit quality. Pre-unblinding goodness-of-fit p-values were only 4–5%.

item.title: MadNIS, Ready for Production at LO
item.dc:creator: Theo Heimel et al.
item.description:
MadNIS now covers full pp processes with all their partonic subprocesses, and it runs untuned from defaults set by a three-iteration VEGAS survey. It will be MadGraph7’s LO default. The main additions are: - learned sampling of symmetry permutations, and of flavour with a PDF prior; - merging of matrix elements, channels and, optionally, subprocesses; - buffered training on partially unweighted events; - concurrent training and generation on GPU.

On an H100 with training excluded (κ_∞), MadNIS beats VEGAS on every benchmark, by 1.27× (tt̅ dileptonic) up to 247× (ℓℓ+3j). Distributions match a sliced MG5aMC baseline in pulls, including the tails.

The amortization numbers the digest flagged look like this for tt̅+nj on an A100. Break-even with VEGAS comes at 9×10⁶, 1.5×10⁵ and 6×10³ events for n=1,2,3, after 8 s, 11 s and 1.4 min of training. At 10³ iterations, the speed-ups are already 2.9, 8.9 and 16.

Caveats: - Training cost of the headline numbers. The process-zoo figures come from trainings of up to 6.7–8.8 h. - Retraining. Any change of process, cuts or parameters requires a new training. - CPU. CPU training is more than 10× slower in wall-clock time. - Open choices. When to merge subprocesses is unresolved, and the defaults are “likely to evolve” (alpha release v0.2.1). - Low multiplicity. At low multiplicity, VEGAS combined with MadSpace mappings already captures most of the gain.

item.title: When hadrons collide: di-J/ψ structure in the final state (Eric S. Swanson (University of Pittsburgh))
item.description:
Swanson gets a χ²/ndf=56/50 fit to the LHCb di-J/ψ spectrum (6.2–7.7 GeV) without introducing any states. The production model is a compact octet–octet ccc̅c̅ source in 2⁺⁺, rescattering through ten charmonium-pair channels. Quark-exchange kernels come from a constituent model whose parameters are fixed by the charmonium spectrum, and the scattering is solved to all orders with a Kohn–Hulthén–Kato resonating-group method.

The structures map onto thresholds: - a J/ψJ/ψ threshold enhancement in the X(6600) region; - a dip from flux lost to the J/ψψ(2S) channel, followed by a peak at 6.9 GeV; - a 7.2 GeV shoulder between the J/ψψ(3S) and ψ(2S)ψ(2S) thresholds.

Only three background parameters are free (a, c, λ), with DPS fixed to LHCb’s template. The fit needs both an incoherent remainder (c=0 gives 90/51) and a corrected continuum slope (λ=0 gives 152/51). The amplitude has poles at 6809-68i and 7102-57i MeV. Swanson argues these reflect a repulsive-shell/attractive-core interaction rather than tetraquarks.

Caveats: - CMS fit. CMS is fitted less well (117/55), and its dips are deeper than the model’s. - Missing and spurious features. The model undershoots the 6.9 GeV peak by 15–20% and predicts an unobserved ψ(2S)ψ(2S) bump near 7.4 GeV. - Omitted physics. Quark annihilation is left out, which removes absorption into D⁽)D̅⁽). J/ψψ(3770) is excluded because it couples only through tensor forces. - ΥΥ test. The prediction gives broad features at 19.3 and 19.7 GeV and a sharp dip near 20.05 GeV. Because an earlier loop-cusp model predicted the same enhancements, this tests threshold rescattering in general, not this model specifically.

item.title: Complete four-loop pressure of cold QED
item.dc:creator: Aapeli K\"arkk\"ainen et al.
item.description:
The N³LO pressure of cold, dense massless QED (jellium setup) is now complete, the first new order since Freedman–McLerran in 1977. The soft and mixed sectors were already known, so the missing piece was the hard contribution: 10 four-loop 1PI vacuum diagrams at finite μ. The authors generated them in general R_ξ gauge and confirmed that the gauge dependence cancels. Canonicalization reduces O(10⁵⁾ scalar integrals to 75 masters, compared with 114 in QCD. The methods were: - cutting rules and self-energy techniques for the factorizable topologies, - IBP plus differential equations as a cross-check on a subset, - thermal loop-tree duality (LTD) Monte Carlo for roughly 70% of the integrals, at about 10⁶ CPU-core hours.

The hard IR pole cancels exactly against the mixed sector. The new constant term is p_3,5=1.02270(2)-5.64(5)N_f⁻¹⁻⁸.50(7)N_f⁻². Two independent checks hold up: - The Bugblatter sum gives b=-5.44(24)×10⁻⁷, against the literature value -5.545(12)×10⁻⁷. - Renormalization-group invariance holds through N³LO.

Along the way the authors corrected two errors in their earlier work: an O(ε) normalization error in the mixed term, and a factor of two in the N²LO handling that shifted p_3,4.

The physics result is the uncertainty story. At α_e=0.2, order-to-order shifts far exceed the X∈[1/2,2] scale band. The Bayesian abc error band at N²LO, by contrast, contains the actual N³LO result near its center, and the series stays predictive up to α_e≈0.4. Because the physical α is small, the direct phenomenology is negligible. The value is as a benchmark and as a partial integral library for cold quark matter, and hence for the neutron-star EoS. One caveat is that the Bayesian conclusion rests on modelling the coefficients as draws from a common distribution.

item.title: Threshold enhancement in π⁰π⁰ from ψ(3686)→π⁰π⁰J/ψ
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
BESIII selects 8.4×10⁶ events from 2.7×10⁹ ψ(3686) decays, using J/ψ→ee,μμ and a 7C kinematic fit. Background is about 0.1% and non-peaking. A Breit–Wigner fit to the threshold structure gives: - 2554 ± 62 signal events, at more than 10σ, - M=274.3±2.1±0.6 MeV, - Γ=17.1±1.5±0.5 MeV.

These values are consistent with the charged channel (about 283 MeV and 17 MeV). The neutral mode carries no I=1 component and no ISR background, which makes it the cleaner confirmation.

The unfolded 2D spectrum, in m_ππ and cosθ_π⁰, discriminates between models: - ChPT: adding FSI improves χ²/ndf from 48.6 to 6.5, but the model still misses the threshold region. - QCDME: with 2S–1D mixing fixed at θ_mix=12^∘ and FSI included, it describes the full spectrum. - Adler zero: the dip near 0.3 GeV persists, which BESIII ties to the Adler zero.

Caveats: - The mixing angle had to be fixed because it is strongly correlated with β. - A systematic trend remains in the cosθ pulls. - The ChPT parameter errors are implausibly tiny (e.g. g_1/g_0=-0.09426±0.00002). - The introduction says a structure near the π⁺π⁻ threshold would favor a rescattering cusp, but the paper never states whether the measured mass supports that reading. That question is left to theorists.

item.title: Redshift-space galaxy power spectrum at two loops
item.dc:creator: Oliver H. E. Philcox
item.description:
(The extracted text stops partway through the numerical section; the validation numbers below come from the abstract.)

Philcox gives the first complete two-loop, redshift-space galaxy P(k) in the EFT of large-scale structure (EFTofLSS). The model is renormalized at fifth order in fields and derivatives, and its ingredients are: - 17 leading-gradient, 7 next-to-leading-gradient and 1 next-to-next-to-leading-gradient bias operators, - spatially non-local counterterms generated by the dark-matter equations of motion, - 15 redshift-space counterterm combinations, - 6 stochastic terms.

That totals 49 coefficients, against 10 at one loop. Closure under renormalization is verified exactly at every power of f. IR resummation is applied without the usual factorized approximation. The same kernels fix the deterministic one-loop bispectrum and trispectrum, and 18 of the coefficients are constrained by the one-loop bispectrum.

The loop integrals are precomputed with vegas, so a likelihood evaluation takes milliseconds. On simulations, k_max rises from 0.2 to 0.34 h/Mpc for an LRG sample at z = 0.5. The new biases and counterterms absorb most of the added information, however, and σ_8 does not tighten appreciably. The author also stresses strong parameter degeneracies. On its own the result is a template and a calibration of two-loop expectations, not yet a cosmology gain. Its main promise is in joint fits with higher-order statistics.

(No full text was provided for the other two picks, CMS arXiv:2610.13634 and Lee et al. arXiv:2610.13930, so they are omitted here.)

item.title: Evidence for Normal Neutrino Ordering with Combined Atmospheric Neutrino Experiments
item.dc:creator: Miaochen Jin et al.
item.description:
Inverted ordering is excluded at 3.3σ using atmospheric data alone. Only 2 of 4397 IO pseudoexperiments exceed the observed χ²_IO-χ²_NO=11.0. The Clopper–Pearson 68% interval on that tail fraction gives Z∈[3.08,3.60]σ, and the more conservative CL_s gives 2.55σ. The ingredients are: - Super-K I–V (pure water), with an independent high-statistics GENIE Monte Carlo and a bug-fixed SK release confirmed by the collaboration. - IceCube-DeepCore, 8 years. - ORCA6.

Flux and cross-section nuisances (39 of 143) are shared across experiments. The individual preferences (Δχ²⁼⁶.2, 1.6, 0.5) add coherently via mantle/core MSW and parametric resonances at 2–10 GeV. Relative to a trivial χ² sum, the correlated treatment tightens Δm²_31 by 19% and sin²θ_23 by 9%. Results: Δm²_31=2.44⁺⁰.06_-0.04×10⁻³ eV² (2.2%), sin²θ_23=0.52 with Δχ²⁼⁰.3 between octants, and δ_CP=1.30⁺⁰.24_-0.28π (≈0.3π disfavoured at >2.7σ). The atmospheric contours sit closer to T2K than to NOvA. The authors estimate that adding JUNO’s Δm²_31 gives Δχ²≃16, near 4σ, but that figure still needs joint pseudoexperiments.

Caveats. - The overall goodness of fit is p=0.011, driven by ORCA6; it rises to 0.12 once finite Monte Carlo statistics are included. - The parameter goodness-of-fit test shows 2.2σ inter-experiment tension. IceCube and ORCA6 worsen by 13.7 and 9.6 in χ² at the combined best fit. - The shared CCQE normalization is pulled by −2.5σ. - θ_13 is fixed, and the ORCA energy-scale nuisance is absent. - The δ_CP constraint draws more on data residuals than on the Asimov expectation. - This is a combination of public data, not a collaboration result.

item.title: Reassessing the X(2370) in J/ψ→γK_S⁰K_S⁰π⁰
item.dc:creator: Xiang-Kun Dong et al.
item.description:
A coherent coupled-channel fit does not require an X(2370) in K_S⁰K_S⁰π⁰. The fit uses a 12-channel K-matrix with dispersive loops, applied to digitized BESIII data: - two-dimensional mass maps (6264 KK bins and 6006 Kπ bins); - the parent-mass spectrum.

Adding an eighth bare state near 2.37 GeV lowers the deviance by only 1.26% (7926.4→7826.6, with 16 extra parameters), and the projected line shapes are nearly identical. The extra pole sits at 2424-i 149 MeV, twice as broad as the PDG reference 2377-i 74. Its identification with X(2370) is unclear.

The physics consequence is for the flavor-singlet argument. If the true X(2370)→KK̅π yield is smaller than the 1D fits imply, the denominator of BESIII’s ℛ<0.081 shrinks. The small K^*K̅ yield would then no longer demonstrate selective suppression, which weakens the glueball and η_c-analogy readings without excluding them.

Caveats, stated by the authors. - Bin contents are reconstructed from a colour palette, with no inter-distribution correlations, efficiency, or resolution. - No significance or pole uncertainties are quoted. - Only mesonic channels are modelled, so the ΣΣ̅ interpretation is not tested. - K_0^(1430) parameters were tuned within their uncertainties. - The J/ψ→K^0K̅^*0 background is not modelled.

item.title: Observation of s-channel single top-quark production at 13 TeV with ATLAS
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description: (Abstract only.) ATLAS reports the first single-experiment observation of s-channel single top, at 5.1σ observed (5.2σ expected). The dataset is 140 fb⁻¹, with events selected for exactly one lepton, missing E_T, and exactly two b-jets. A GNN separates the signal from tt̅, W+jets and t-channel backgrounds, and a likelihood fit to its output gives σ_tb̅+t̅b=10.8±1.5 (stat)±1.6 (syst) pb, consistent with the SM. The comparable statistical and systematic errors suggest further gains will need systematic reductions as well as more data. The abstract does not quote the SM prediction or a |V_tb| interpretation.

item.title: A gauge-invariant measure for lattice chiral fermions
item.dc:creator: Nathaniel Craig
item.description:
Craig claims a nonperturbative, smooth, exponentially local, gauge-invariant overlap-fermion measure for SU(5) with 10⊕5̅. He extends it to all four global forms [SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1)]/Γ_SM, Γ_SM=1,ℤ_2,ℤ_3,ℤ_6, by embedding SM links into SU(5).

The key move replaces Lüscher’s abelian interpolation of the gauge potential to zero, which can exit the admissible domain for nonabelian fields. Instead:

  • A smooth connection is reconstructed from U and sampled at auxiliary spacings h_n=3⁻ⁿ, with fine plaquettes obeying 1-(F_hU)(p)≤Cεh².
  • Hermitian Wilson operators at successive spacings are interpolated linearly. The intermediate operators are not link fields, and a uniform gap g is proved throughout.
  • Each step contributes a curvature-strip term B_n, and the measure term is 𝔏=∑_n B_n.
  • Return phases telescope. An exact colour-trace identity for 10⊕5̅ cancels the leading terms, which makes the sum converge.
  • Global integrability on noncontractible loops uses an auxiliary SU(3) connection under which the fermions pair conjugately.

The general sufficient conditions are cubic-anomaly cancellation plus even multiplicity of half-integer-isospin representations under an SU(2)⊂SU(N_c). The author says the latter is an artefact of the method.

Where “admissible” bites: - The construction requires a sufficiently small plaquette bound ε. It is volume-independent but not quantified in the extracted text. - The measure is fixed only up to one constant phase per connected component of admissible fields. The current’s transformation laws do not guarantee that every choice of these relative phases respects discrete symmetries.

The convergence, locality and gap estimates sit in appendices not included in the extract. Lean verification is relegated to supplementary material. As the digest notes, this is an existence construction, not a simulation algorithm.

item.title: Is the Light Neutralino Dark Matter Still Viable in the MSSM After the LZ-2024 Results?
item.dc:creator: Zhiyang Bao et al.
item.description:
LZ-2024 excludes the sub-100 GeV Bino h-funnel at Z>5.9 (p=1.8×10⁻⁹) and the Z-funnel at Z>4.1 (p=2.1×10⁻⁵). The result holds for Ωh²⁼⁰.12 and for 0.06 (half the dark matter), without imposing the LHC bound μ≳760 GeV.

The argument rests on one coupling (C_h or C_Z) setting both annihilation and scattering. Finite mediator width and thermal smearing cap ⟨σv⟩, so the relic density imposes a floor on σ^SI or σ^SD_n.

The analysis is deliberately conservative: - Loop corrections: full one-loop vertex corrections (904 diagrams) give K^SI≲1.5 and K^SD_n≲1.3. Scale variation changes these corrections by at most 5%. - Hadronic inputs: FLAG-2024 values (σ_πN=42.2±2.4 MeV) are used, with worst-case 3σ rescalings of 0.78 (SI) and 0.62 (SD) applied at every point. The authors note that the Roy–Steiner value σ_πN≃58–59 MeV would only raise σ^SI.

The resulting cross-section floors sit nearly an order of magnitude above the LZ-2024 limits. LZ-2022 gave only Z<2.

Caveats: - The LZ-2024 recast is micrOMEGAs’ background-free Poisson model. It is calibrated near 90% CL and then extrapolated far into the tail. - DDCalc implements only LZ-2022. There, micrOMEGAs underestimates Z, which supports the claim that the micrOMEGAs numbers are conservative. - Near-degenerate Higgsino–Wino points (splitting <3 GeV) were cut for counterterm instability.

What remains for a thermal Bino is coannihilation, heavy-Higgs resonance or well-tempering, which together point to |m_χ̃|≳200 GeV.

item.title: Can Nuclear Recoils and Solar Neutrinos Resolve the Composition of Singlino-Higgsino Dark Matter?
item.dc:creator: Jingwei Lian et al.
item.description:
Abstract only. The paper’s point is a degeneracy: swapping ground and excited states can leave an inelastic recoil spectrum unchanged while shifting ground-state annihilation by orders of magnitude. Solar-neutrino signals from captured dark matter then distinguish compositions that recoils cannot.

Applied in the NMSSM to fits of the high-energy LZ candidate, the analysis finds: - Disfavoured: Higgsino-pair inelastic fits overproduce solar signals. - Solar-compatible: singlino ground states, and Higgsino ground states with weak inelastic transitions. - Escape route: an elastic Higgsino alternative evades the solar bound by closing the inelastic transition that drives capture.

The abstract gives no quantitative limits. The authors acknowledge residual degeneracies tied to annihilation, halo and detector assumptions.

item.title: Molecular Structure Effects in Low-Lying P-wave Bottom-Strange Meson Spectrum
item.dc:creator: Wei Hao et al.
item.description:
A compact bs̅ picture cannot reach the B_s0^(5700): the plain confinement+OGE model puts the 0⁺ at 5851 MeV. One-loop (α_s²) corrections to the OGE potential lower it only to 5816 MeV, still ~120 MeV above LHCb’s 5698.9±1.5±0.6 MeV. Coupling the bare state to BK/B^K via ³P_0 vertices supplies the missing shift and brings the 0⁺ to 5727 MeV, within ~30 MeV of data. Near-threshold phase-space suppression accounts for the narrow width. The same machinery puts the 1⁺ partner at 5755 MeV (B^K-dominated), close to Nowak–Zahed’s chiral-doubling 5747±2 MeV. The j_ℓ=3/2 states stay essentially compact. The authors give E1 widths of 45 keV for B_s0^→B_s^γ and ~55–58 keV for the 1⁺→B_s⁽)γ modes, which they propose as the Run 3 discovery channels.

Caveats: - Molecular content not quantified. The paper does not report a B_s⁰π⁰ width. That is today’s discriminating number against Albaladejo et al. and Sánchez-Illana et al. It also gives no explicit compositeness, despite promising to quantify the admixture. - Radiative widths may be mislabeled. The quoted 58/55 keV values come from the Table 4 rows for B’_s1(1P). The B_s1(1P) rows, which correspond to the state assigned to 5747 in Table 3, give 50.9/34.6 keV. - Bare-state wavefunctions. All radiative widths use quark-model wavefunctions, not the dressed ones. - B_s2^ width is a fit, not a test.The ³P_0 strengtγ_0 was fitted to the B_s2^*(5840) width, so reproducing its 1.5 MeV is not an independent check. - Residual offset. The 0⁺ still misses by ~30 MeV.

item.title: Fully charmed tetraquarks on the Lattice with controlled errors
item.dc:creator: Zhenyu Zhang et al.
item.description:
The headline result is a J^P=0⁺ ccc̅c̅ state at 5934.8(13) MeV, 33.2(13) MeV below η_cη_c, and therefore strong-decay-stable. The authors discretize a standard OGE+linear potential model on a periodic lattice and diagonalize it with Lanczos (“LQPM”). This is a lattice-discretized quark model, not lattice QCD. Benchmarks are good: - η_c, J/ψ and the 2S states land within a few MeV of experiment. - Ω_ccc=4817.3(9) MeV agrees with NNQS and lies below the variational GEM value of 4823.

They also find a 1⁺ only 10.9 MeV below η_cJ/ψ, which they flag as potential-dependent. The 2⁺ sits 24 MeV above J/ψJ/ψ, and they connect it to the CMS near-threshold 2⁺ structure. A bound 0⁺ contradicts essentially every prior model, including DeepQuark. The authors attribute their ~500 MeV lower masses to enforcing full antisymmetry with non-symmetric spatial parts. Restricting to symmetric spatial functions recovers NNQS (~6414–6508 MeV).

The “controlled errors” claim deserves scrutiny: - Coarse spacing. The tetraquark is computed at a≈0.2 fm, a spacing at which the supplement says charmonium has not converged. Finer spacings “do not converge.” - Threshold mismatch. The quoted 5968 MeV threshold equals twice the fine-lattice η_c mass. The text does not show it evaluated at a≈0.2 fm. - Small boxes, poor fits. Only five boxes are used, up to 1.8 fm. The extrapolation adds 16 MeV beyond the largest box, and the fits have χ²/dof=15–28. The ±1.3 MeV error is fit-only. - Scattering-like color structure. The color ratio converges to the 2:1 value characteristic of meson–meson scattering states.

item.title: Relations between electroweak parameters to order α_s³
item.dc:creator: Andreas Maier et al.
item.description:
Maier and Marquard complete the top-mediated four-loop QCD corrections to Δr̅ and Δκ beyond the leading Δρ term. They supply the missing pieces: - the four-loop flavour-singlet polarization functions; - top-mass corrections to the bb correlator; - a sixth low-energy term in the axial correlator.

The expansion in M_Z²/m_t² is taken to M_Z¹⁰/m_t¹⁰, with negligible truncation error. The new α_s³ m_t^≤0 terms shift M_W by ≈ −0.8 MeV with an on-shell top mass and ≈ −0.2 MeV in MS. For comparison, FCC-ee projects 0.16 MeV systematic and 0.18 MeV statistical uncertainty, so these terms are relevant at that precision.

Two points matter for projections: - Scheme dependence. In MS the subleading α_s³m̅_t⁰ term (−0.22 MeV) exceeds the formally leading α_s³m̅_t² term (−0.03 MeV). The factor-of-four scheme spread at this order is itself a theory uncertainty at the FCC-ee scale. - Five loops needed. Extrapolating the on-shell pattern, the authors expect α_s⁴ M_t² to contribute several hundred keV. That makes five-loop ρ desirable.

Scope is pure QCD on top/bottom loops, and the numerical study neglects the Δr–Δr̅ difference. Results are supplied in electronic form.

item.title: Stars Would Remember a Recent Gravitational Transition: Testing G-step Resolutions of the Hubble Tension with Red Dwarfs
item.dc:creator: Jeremy Sakstein et al.
item.description:
Both Hubble-motivated G-step benchmarks are disfavoured: ΔG/G_0=+0.04 at 73 Myr (EGSM) at 3.1σ, and +0.11 at 130 Myr (OGSM) at 4.0σ. The profile likelihood has its minimum at ΔG=0 for both transition times.

The mechanism is a radius memory in fully convective red dwarfs. Homology gives an equilibrium radius R∝G⁰.324, while the fast adiabatic response gives R∝G⁻¹. The perturbation then relaxes on t_relax≃0.05 t_KH∼10⁸ yr, which is comparable to the proposed look-back times. A drop from larger G therefore leaves today’s stars inflated.

The analysis uses: - MESA tracks with an implemented G-step; - a per-star starspot covering fraction treated as a nuisance parameter; - eight CHEOPS detached-eclipsing-binary M dwarfs (0.1–0.31 M_⊙, periods ≥5 d) with mass–radius correlations ρ=0.53–0.90.

This gives Δχ²⁼⁹.52 (EGSM) and 16.41 (OGSM). Because the spot fractions sit at their physical boundary, the significances come from a parametric bootstrap rather than Wilks’ theorem.

The test is independent of the disputed solar and terrestrial modelling arguments.

Caveats: - Boundary stars drive the result. All of the leverage comes from the four stars pinned at f_spot=0, where spots can no longer absorb the extra inflation. - One star dominates. Dropping J2343+29 cuts the significances to 2.45σ (EGSM) and 1.90σ (OGSM). - Model systematics matter. A coherent 1% downward shift of the model radii lowers Δχ² to 5.72 and 10.92. - Only positive steps are tested. Both benchmarks have ΔG>0.

item.title: Violation and Restoration of Probability Positivity in Perturbative QFT
item.dc:creator: Bin Gong et al.
item.description:
The central argument concerns exclusive processes with colourless and neutral external states. There, each renormalized loop amplitude is IR-finite on its own and no KLN sum over unresolved states is needed. Gong et al. conclude that truncating the squared amplitude is an inherited QED habit, and that |∑_l≤M𝒜⁽l)|² is the right observable.

They recast eleven published NNLO results in the form Γ=Γ_LO|1+a_s(c_1+ic_2)+a_s²⁽c_3+ic_4)|². In every case both complex coefficients have modulus below 1, with the largest, 0.67, for J/ψ+η_c. Selected ratios Γ/Γ_LO at NLO, NNLO:

Channel Amplitude-level Squared-level
J/ψ→3γ 0.276, 0.126 −0.02, −0.44
Υ→3γ 0.426, 0.190 0.28, −0.11
e⁺e⁻→J/ψJ/ψ 0.40, 0.058 0.26, −0.38

J/ψ→3γ goes negative at NLO in the traditional expansion. Υ→3γ and double-J/ψ go negative at NNLO. Zhan et al. apply the same prescription to ultraperipheral J/ψ+γ.

Caveats, visible in the paper itself: - Partial higher orders. The NLO square keeps |ℳ_1|² but not the same-order 2Re(ℳ_0^*ℳ_2), so it contains incomplete 𝒪(α_s²⁾ terms. - Convergence is judged inside the modulus. The rates themselves still fall sharply from NLO to NNLO: by a factor 2.2 for J/ψ→3γ and about 7 for double J/ψ. - Positivity is not accuracy. Positivity is guaranteed by construction, which does not show the result is closer to the true value. - Mostly a reframing. The numbers re-express the group’s own earlier calculations, with α_s re-chosen for the B-factory channels.

item.title: Angular Observables in the Λ_b→Λνν̅ Decay
item.dc:creator: Wolfgang Altmannshofer et al.
item.description:
The full cascade Λ_b→Λ(→pπ⁻⁾νν̅ is described by five angular coefficients, S_1–4 and A_5; all but S_1 need Λ_b polarization. Z-pole Λ_b supply it: LEP measured 𝒫=-0.40±0.14.

The coefficients split by what they probe: - Chirality: S_1 and S_2 go as |C_R|²⁻|C_L|², which the mesonic modes cannot see. - CP phase: A_5 is a T-odd CP asymmetry proportional to Im(C_LC_R^*), with no flavour tagging or time dependence needed.

Mesonic data fix only |C_L±C_R|, so they confine the couplings to a ring via (|C_R|²⁻|C_L|²⁾²⁺⁴⁽Im C_LC_R^*)²⁼|C_R+C_L|²|C_R-C_L|². The baryonic observables pick the point on that ring.

SM predictions: - branching ratio (7.59±1.03)×10⁻⁶, dominated by form-factor and CKM uncertainties; - ⟨S_1⟩=-0.926±0.018; - an S_2 zero crossing at 12.6±1.2 GeV² that is independent of the Wilson coefficients, and so tests the form factors.

Projected FCC-ee reach, assuming a 10% branching-ratio measurement: - Real couplings: S_1 and S_2 break the four-fold real-coupling degeneracy even at ±0.5 uncertainty on the angular observables. - Complex couplings: at ±0.1 all four benchmarks are distinguishable from the SM. At ±0.5 the A_5 sensitivity is largely lost and only the pure right-handed benchmark survives.

This bears directly on the Belle II K⁺νν̅ excess, which the authors put about 2.7σ above the SM.

Caveats: - No dedicated angular estimates. The ±0.1–0.5 uncertainties are assumed scans. - Simplified meson comparison. The mesonic side is a 5% toy estimate. - Only right-handed currents show up. A pure rescaling of C_L leaves every angular observable unchanged. - Dark-sector explanations not covered. Light invisible states are explicitly excluded, although several Belle II interpretations rely on them.

item.title: Third-Order Logarithmic Resummation for Jet-Vetoed Higgs Production
item.dc:creator: Samuel Abreu et al.
item.description:
The first N³LL+N³LO prediction for the gluon-fusion zero-jet cross section gives 30.11 (+3.2%/−3.0%) pb at p_T^v=30 GeV, with R=0.4 anti-k_t jets at 13.6 TeV. That is ~3% above fixed-order N³LO (29.24 pb). The shift lies outside N³LO’s narrow +0.7/−2.2% scale band, so fixed-order scale variation alone misses the logarithmic correction. Relative to NNLL+NNLO, the central value rises ~4% and the uncertainty shrinks from 6–8% to ~3%. The new ingredient is the three-loop, algorithm-dependent rapidity anomalous dimension γ_ν⁽³⁾⁽R²⁾ from the companion paper, combined with the four-loop cusp, three-loop γ_V and two-loop boundary terms, all implemented in RadISH. The authors tested the expansion against NNLOJet H+jet with M=1 TeV and R=0.1. With Δγ_ν⁽³⁾ set to zero, the expansion visibly fails to converge, so the three-loop clustering term is numerically essential.

The physics point is that the previous NNLL+N³LO result had an accidental cancellation near 30 GeV. N³LL lifts it and restores a uniform 3–4% third-order correction for p_T^v≳20 GeV. Alternative matching schemes and log-switching prescriptions all agree within the band. The code is public (JetVHeto).

Caveats: - Missing effects: top and bottom mass effects and small-R resummation are not included. Both were 1–2% in earlier work, comparable to the quoted uncertainty. - ln R terms: the authors flag large subleading lnR terms in γ_ν⁽³⁾ as motivation for lnR resummation. - Factorization breaking: coherence-violating effects, which break factorization from five loops, are explicitly set aside. The non-global/super-leading front noted in the digest therefore sits outside this calculation.

item.title: First observation of electron antineutrinos from nuclear reactors at Super-Kamiokande (K. Abe (The Super-Kamiokande Collaboration) et al.)
item.description:
SK-Gd sees reactor ν̅_e via IBD with Gd-tagged neutrons. The exposure is 411.52 live days: SK-VI at 0.011% Gd and SK-VII at 0.033% Gd. The no-reactor hypothesis gives Δχ²⁼³⁴.7, about 6σ, and the oscillated fit has χ²⁼¹⁶.7/16.

Reactor-only fit, with θ_13 fixed: - sin²θ_12=0.500±0.155 - Δm²_21=(9.08⁺⁰.55_-0.54)×10⁻⁵ eV²

Comparison with SK solar. SK’s own solar fit gives Δm²_21=(6.10⁺¹.26_-0.86)×10⁻⁵ eV². The differences are 1.1σ in θ_12 and 2.2σ in Δm²_21. A parameter-goodness-of-fit test gives 1.9σ compatibility. The main text quotes Δχ²_PG=7.25 (p=0.027) while the appendix quotes 7.64 (p=0.022), a minor internal inconsistency. The combined SK fit is sin²θ_12=0.332, Δm²_21=(8.94⁺⁰.46_-0.47)×10⁻⁵ eV².

Why it matters: this is a new water-Cherenkov reactor handle on the solar sector, from the same detector that measures solar neutrinos. That makes it an internal CPT-motivated cross-check, and a demonstration of Gd-water for low-energy ν̅_e.

The paper does not quantify the digest’s “~3σ above JUNO” framing. It calls its values consistent with global fits and recent reactor results, JUNO included.

Caveats: - Background model: the accidental background comes from a single low-reactor window (Nov–Dec 2020) and is statistics-limited. - Flux inputs: fluxes use electrical rather than thermal load factors. - Systematics: neutron-capture γ modeling (5.4%) and coincidence efficiency (5.5%) dominate the listed systematics.

item.title: Higgsino dark matter compatible with the LZ high-energy nuclear-recoil event and IceCube constraints
item.dc:creator: Katherine Freese et al.
item.description:
Heavy Higgsinos can explain the 248 keV LZ event without violating IceCube solar bounds, but the thermal 1.1 TeV case barely survives. The authors build a 96-bin approximate LZ likelihood digitized from LZ’s published data, calibrated with 30k toys, which reproduces LZ’s interval near δ=350 keV. They include the corrected (4× larger) inelastic cross section.

Thermal 1.1 TeV case. The LZ-compatible splitting depends on the halo model: - SHM: 360–370 keV. - SHM+LMC: 485–505 keV.

IceCube lower bounds on δ at 1.1 TeV depend on how captured Higgsinos cool in the Sun:

Cooling assumption Lower bound on δ
Capture–annihilation equilibrium imposed 566 keV
Inelastic + elastic SD 558 keV
Inelastic only 506 keV

The thermal Higgsino survives only at δ≈508 keV, and only under three conditions together: LMC tail included, all elastic cooling neglected, and the LZ sideband dropped. The authors call this a limiting case rather than a robust interpretation.

Heavier Higgsinos. The key novelty is the m_χ⁻² falloff of the elastic SD cross section, which weakens cooling at high mass. With it, compatible regions open at: - ~2 TeV (δ~520 keV) for SHM+LMC, no sideband and SD-only elastic cooling. - ≳10–30 TeV (δ≈350–400 keV) for the SHM. - Equilibrium imposed everywhere: ≳80 TeV for the SHM, and 13–120 TeV (465–520 keV) for SHM+LMC.

They also find Sommerfeld resonances near 6.5, 25 and 55 TeV that locally tighten the bounds.

Caveats: - Halo model: the LMC tail uses a single simulated halo with a large LMC/MW mass ratio (0.27). - Sideband acceptance: unpublished, and LZ has not calibrated its nuclear-recoil response there. - Solar treatment: cooling assumes stationary nuclei, radial orbits and a uniform-density population. - IceCube conversion: the W⁺W⁻ limits are frozen above 10 TeV, so high-mass regions are extrapolations. - Cosmology: heavier Higgsinos need a non-standard abundance history.

item.title: Fractional anomalous determinants and the chiral phase transition
item.dc:creator: Robert D. Pisarski
item.description:
Pisarski proposes a “syncretic” chiral Lagrangian whose anomalous sector changes across T_χ. Below T_χ, topological charge is taken to be fractional in units of 1/N_c, so terms ℱ_j(Φ^†Φ) [(Φ)^j/N_c+h.c.] appear. The prefactors are fractional powers of Φ^†Φ, chosen so that each term behaves like Φ² as Φ→0. Above T_χ, only integer powers survive. The argument rests on assuming that in the Veneziano limit the free energy depends on θ/N_c. This yields a Witten–Veneziano generalization to arbitrary N_f/N_c in which the η’ stays massive at T_χ without a large ξ_1Φ.
