The predicted transition order by flavor number: - N_f=1: crossover (Z(2)-like). - N_f=2: second order, O(4). - N_f=3: still first order because the cubic Φ remains, but possibly very weakly so, since ξ_1 can be small. - N_f=4: a 𝒬=2/3 term could induce a weak, Halperin–Lubensky–Ma-type first-order transition.

The model is motivated by lattice data that find no first-order signal for N_f=3. One example is Zhang et al.’s susceptibility scaling exponent α≈0.39±0.04, which fits neither first order (α=3) nor Z(2) (α≈1.96). Another is the measured b_2≈-0.19/N_c², read here as a dense liquid of fractional instantons. The proposed test is to fit the 2+1-flavor ratio ℛ_π,a_0(T) to σ_s⁴/3,σ_s²/3,σ_s between 150 and 300 MeV.

Caveats are substantial, and the author flags them himself: - The ℱ_j are unknown, and the ansatz is called “rank supposition.” FRG work already indicates additional invariants are needed. - The non-degenerate case relevant to the proposed lattice test is deferred to a separate paper. - QCD is “blithely” assumed close to the Veneziano limit.

item.title: Drell–Yan lepton pair production from low to high transverse momentum
item.dc:creator: Beno\^it Assi et al.
item.description:
The prediction is N³LO matched to approximate N⁴LL′ q_T resummation, with unknown four-loop boundary terms estimated in large-β_0. Its main novelty is the nonperturbative input. The Collins–Soper kernel is taken from continuum-limit lattice QCD over 0.15≲b_T≲0.8 fm, giving c_0=0.032±0.012 GeV² at B_NP=2 GeV⁻¹. The only parameter fitted to Drell–Yan data is a Gaussian width, κ_NP=3.0±0.5 GeV⁻².

Comparison with ATLAS 13 TeV data: - Agreement: deviations are at most 1.3% below 10 GeV, 2.0% for 10–30 GeV, and 3.5% above 30 GeV, with χ²/bin of 0.2, 1.0 and 1.6 in those regions. - Lattice uncertainty: the c_0 uncertainty contributes up to 2.6% in the first bin and at most 0.8% elsewhere.

The calculation is transferred to event samples by maximum-entropy reweighting. Of 170 tabulated moments in r_T and ϕ_acop, 14–19 are selected, giving event-local multipliers ∝exp(∑λ_j g_j) that are strictly positive. - Sherpa: the reweighted sample matches the calculation to about 2% in a typical bin, against a prior that was off by up to 40%. The effective sample size is essentially unchanged (7.6% → 7.3%). - POWHEG: agreement is about 3% in a typical bin, with effective sample size held at 99%. The largest deviation from data below 200 GeV falls from 19% to 6%.

Caveats: - The prediction is about 8× less precise than the data in a typical bin, and PDF uncertainties (a few percent) are assessed elsewhere. - The moment covariance is treated as diagonal. - Positivity applies to the multiplier; the Sherpa prior itself retains signed weights. - Between 200 and 900 GeV the ungated POWHEG weight overshoots the data by 4–40%. - Extension to W production is proposed but not done, which matters for any m_W application.

item.title: Near Threshold Kaluza-Klein Graviton Decays and the Dark Dimension
item.dc:creator: Kevin Langhoff
item.description:
On shell, the massive cubic KK-graviton vertex reduces to the double copy of the Yang–Mills vertex evaluated at massive momenta. The mass term cancels against the terms, and the cancellation follows from the field redefinition h=e^H-1. As a result the amplitude vanishes at threshold, and the decay is pure d-wave with Γ∝p⁵∝Q⁵/2. Relative to the s-wave rate assumed in the dark-dimension cascade literature, the suppression is ∼(Q/μ)²∼10⁻²⁴ for Q∼1 meV and GeV parents.

Consequences for the flat dark dimension: - Cascade: summing over a flat tower with the completeness bound on g_mnℓ saturated, the mass-distribution peak moves by less than 0.1% by matter–radiation equality (δn=100, R=0.05–0.2 μm). - Dark matter: GeV-scale gravitons then live only ∼10⁵ yr, which excludes KK gravitons as the dark matter. - Irreducible background: freeze-in still produces ρ_h/ρ_DM=1.3×10⁻⁶⁽T_RH/5 MeV)³⁽m_KK/5 meV)⁻¹. COMPTEL and EGRET MeV gamma-ray data then cap T_RH. - Combined bound: with T_RH≥5.96 MeV from BBN+CMB+BAO, a viable window survives only for R≲0.2 μm (m_KK≳1 eV). That is roughly three orders of magnitude below the R∼Λ⁻¹/4 expectation.

Caveats: the analysis covers flat or weakly warped geometries only, and the cascade estimate uses a saturated coupling bound. The threshold suppression was found independently by Lee, Randall and Riojas (the Wednesday paper). A factor-10 improvement in MeV telescopes such as AMEGO-X or e-ASTROGAM would tighten the bound further.

item.title: 𝒪(αα_s²⁾ corrections to the Top Quark mass
item.dc:creator: Daniele Gaggero et al.
item.description:
The first three-loop mixed QCD–EW term in the top pole-to-MS relation shifts m_t(M_t) by −216 MeV at M_t=172.3 GeV. The pure 𝒪(α_s³⁾ term shifts it by −554 MeV, so the mixed term is about 0.5% of the “NLO” result, comparable to the QCD piece. The total NLO→NNLO shift is −770 MeV, leaving M_t-m_t⁽ⁿ⁼²⁾⁽M_t)=106 MeV. Across the full M_t range the shift is a steady ~200 MeV, against the ATLAS+CMS uncertainty of ±0.33 GeV. The calculation uses the Jegerlehner–Kalmykov scheme with tadpoles kept, so the MS mass is gauge invariant. Master integrals are built in ϵ-factorized form. The W topologies contain the two-loop-sunrise elliptic period, and the Z/H topologies contain the three-loop equal-mass banana. Several required forms do not survive into the physical result: the weight-four modular form and ℱ_1. γ_5 traces in the χ-Goldstone diagrams are handled with local counterterms. The authors check the RGE-predicted poles, the Yukawa consistency of the single pole, and the NNLO QCD top width extracted from the imaginary part.

Why it matters: the term is the same size as the experimental error. In the effective series that groups the one-loop QCD and EW pieces together, the scale band shrinks from 175.2⁺⁹.2_-7.9 GeV to 172.1⁺².4_-5.0 GeV.

Caveats: the residual band is still several GeV wide and asymmetric. The authors also warn that the known, sizable 𝒪(α²⁾ corrections are left out of their mass-scan plot.

item.title: Unpolarized quasi- and pseudo-distributions at one loop: gluon correlator decomposition, matching, and the region |x|>1
item.dc:creator: Christopher Monahan et al.
item.description:
The Balitsky–Morris–Radyushkin gluon-in-gluon kernel misses a finite polynomial. The polynomial is the same in all three of their index combinations. The authors trace it to one appendix step, where a loop-generated index between the two field strengths is summed over 2 transverse directions instead of d-2. That drops an evanescent operator, which produces exactly the missing polynomial when it multiplies the collinear pole. Their MS result agrees with Yao–Ji–Zhang, and the same polynomial separates Yao–Ji–Zhang from BMR. In ratio-scheme pseudo-PDF extractions, ⟨x⟩_g is protected. The normalized second and third moments, however, come out roughly 11% and 13% too low at α_s=0.3, so the true MS gluon is harder than reported.

The framework splits the correlator into six covariant form factors with a 6×6 mixing matrix. That matrix has three eigenvalue sectors (Z_⊥⊥², Z_⊥⊥Z_∥⊥, Z_∥⊥²), so any lattice index choice follows without new loops. The result is cross-checked in R_ξ and axial gauge.

A second conceptual result uses Paley–Wiener. The |x|>1 exterior comes entirely from the branch point of log(z̃²μ²⁾ at ν=0, and at leading power it is fixed pointwise by the renormalization group. At one loop it is n_f-independent, with tail coefficients 5C_A/6 for ℳ_pp and 11C_A/6 for 𝒢^ziiz. Fitting the exterior with independent parameters therefore risks absorbing power corrections into the leading-twist PDF.

Caveats: the analysis is one-loop only, the moment shifts are an estimate at fixed α_s, and gluon target-mass corrections are not known.

item.title: Constraints on Complex Electroweak WIMPs from Solar Capture
item.dc:creator: Juan P. Luengas et al.
item.description:
Endothermic capture depends only on hypercharge: the Y=1 rate is 4× the Y=1/2 rate. For n≥4, the loop-induced SI elastic scattering (∝n⁴) and the Sommerfeld-enhanced annihilation keep the Sun in equilibrium. The IceCube bound is therefore a single universal curve per Y for fermions and scalars alike.

The excluded splitting is largest at TeV masses, ~600 keV for Y=1 and ~570 keV for Y=1/2, and it falls to 350–400 keV by 100 TeV. Under the SHM this excludes the 3_1, 5_1, 4_1/2 and 6_1/2 as sources of the LZ 248 keV event. The 8_1/2 is marginal. Only the 10_1/2 (158 TeV) and 12_1/2 (253 TeV) survive, because they sit in the heavy-mass LZ island.

The solar curve barely depends on the halo, since capture is dominated by slow particles. The LMC tail instead moves the LZ-preferred δ above 500 keV. Under that tail, 6_1/2 and above become allowed, 4_1/2 is marginal, and 3_1, 5_1 escape IceCube but match LZ only at ~3σ.

For the doublets: - The fermion doublet reproduces the earlier Higgsino bound, δ≲566 keV. - The scalar doublet has no spin-dependent sinking channel and stalls at 0.1–0.2 R_⊙. Its bound peaks near 510 keV and is gone by 10 TeV.

Why it matters: it makes the velocity-tail question decisive for any heavy-multiplet LZ fit.

Caveats: - The fit rests on a single event, and its two mass islands are separated by only 1–2σ. - Sommerfeld factors are parametric, good to ~30% off resonance. - The analysis restricts to Y≤1 and assumes no tree-level Higgs portal for scalars. A portal with λ_χH≳0.01 would strengthen the scalar-doublet bound.

item.title: Measurement of Neutrino Oscillation Parameters at JUNO and Indication of the Neutrino Mass Ordering
item.dc:creator: The JUNO Collaboration
item.description:
JUNO used 207.2 live days, 8,294 IBD candidates, and a 52.5 km mean baseline. It measures Δm²_31 = +2.509⁺⁰.027_-0.025×10⁻³ eV² under NO and -2.482⁺⁰.025_-0.026×10⁻³ eV² under IO, a precision of about 1% with Feldman–Cousins intervals. It also reports sin²θ_12 = 0.3036±0.0064 (2.1%) and Δm²_21 = (7.388±0.078)×10⁻⁵ eV² (1.1%).

This is the first analysis to fold in TAO near-detector data (90,280 IBDs) alongside Daya Bay for the unoscillated spectrum. Three independent groups ran blinded analyses, and their results were consistent.

The mass-ordering statement is a reactor–accelerator tension test. NuFit long-baseline Δm²_31 pulls under each hypothesis give Δχ²_IO-NO = 4.86. Pseudo-experiments that scan δ_CP turn this into p = 0.0197, or 2.1σ one-sided (2.3σ two-sided). An independent Bayesian MCMC gives κ= 10.18.

The caveats are structural: - JUNO alone cannot pick the minimum. Its Δχ² profile has several degenerate local minima in Δm²_31. The Daya Bay constraint is what selects the physical one; JUNO then sets the precision. - The NMO evidence is not JUNO-internal. It rests on the mismatch with long-baseline experiments. - Systematics are starting to matter. Statistics still dominate, but Bi–Po backgrounds and detection efficiency are now significant contributors. - Energy resolution is slightly worse than simulated. It is about 3.5% at the ⁶⁸Ge peak, a bit above the MC prediction.

A by-product is the world’s largest geoneutrino sample, at 73±11 TNU.

item.title: The new LHCb beauty-strange state as the bottom partner of the D_s0^*(2317)
item.dc:creator: Miguel Albaladejo et al.
item.description:
LHCb’s narrow B̅_s⁰π⁰ peak sits at 5698.9±1.5±0.6 MeV, 74 MeV below the B⁻K⁺ threshold, with 343 signal candidates. Two unitarized coupled-channel models were tested against it: - Model I: leading-order Weinberg–Tomozawa plus a bare bs̅ state, fitted to B̅⁽*)K lattice levels. - Model II: NLO HMChPT, with its low-energy constants fixed by charm-sector lattice scattering lengths and carried over by heavy-quark flavor symmetry.

Isospin breaking enters through physical masses, π⁰–η mixing and m_u≠m_d, and adds no free parameters.

Predictions with no LHCb input land 1.1σ (Model II) and 1.3–1.7σ (Model I) from the observed mass. Freeing one parameter (the cutoff Λ or the subtraction constant a_b) reproduces the zero-width reference fit, with χ²/dof = 1.22 for 84 degrees of freedom. The required shifts are about 1.1–1.3σ, and joint fits with the lattice data cost only Δχ²_LQCD ≈ 1.1–2.5.

Properties of the state in the fitted models:

Quantity Model I Model II
B̅K compositeness ~45–50% ~60%
Isospin-violating width 34 keV 82.5 keV
1⁺ partner mass 5748.8 MeV 5751.7 MeV

The factor of two between the widths is a rough measure of model dependence, and radiative decays are not included.

The key point is the 1⁺–0⁺ splitting of 49–52 MeV, which is essentially the B_s^*–B_s mass difference (49.4 MeV). The observed peak therefore cannot discriminate between the two assignments and may contain both states. B̅_s⁰γ searches are the direct test.

The authors are careful on several points: - A good fit does not prove a molecular state. - The lattice inputs are at unphysical quark masses, and the predictions carry no systematic uncertainties. - The same NLO amplitudes are in tension with ALICE Dπ femtoscopy in the charm sector. - The resolution kernel was extracted from LHCb’s published figure.

item.title: The four-loop quark-to-quark splitting function in QCD
item.dc:creator: Thomas Gehrmann et al.
item.description:
This paper gives the first fully analytic, all-x four-loop pure-singlet P_ps⁽³⁾. Combined with the non-singlet result (cited here as the same authors’ arXiv:2604.09534), it completes P_qq at N³LO.

The method follows these steps: 1. Compute off-shell quark operator matrix elements, including mixing with gluon and gauge-variant operators. 2. Reduce integrals by IBP over finite fields and solve differential equations in an auxiliary parameter t to reach high Mellin moments. 3. Fit an ansatz of harmonic sums up to weight six to those moments. 4. Invert the Mellin transform to harmonic polylogarithms up to weight six.

The result reproduces the known fixed moments through n=22. It also reproduces the ζ_3 contribution at n=2 that arises from a spurious (n-2) pole.

New content includes the previously unknown leading-power small-x coefficients of lnx/x and 1/x. There is also a discrepancy with the double-log resummation of Davies et al.: the ζ_2ln⁴ x coefficient lacks a (d_F^abcd)²/N_c term there. The two agree at leading colour, matching the pattern seen in the non-singlet case, and the origin is unexplained.

The practical impact on evolution is modest. The existing moment-based approximation agrees with the exact result within its uncertainties over 10⁻⁵<x<1. The main gain is that the approximation uncertainty for this entry of the evolution matrix is gone, while the gluon entries remain approximate.

The ancillary files include a numerical fit accurate to 10⁻⁵ absolute and 10⁻⁸ relative. The exact γ_qq⁽³⁾ may also help reconstruct γ_gg⁽³⁾ through reciprocity.

item.title: Impact of Helicity–Isospin Convention Matching on the Extraction of α from B⁰→(ρπ)⁰
item.dc:creator: Radek \v{Z}leb\v{c}\'{i}k
item.description:
Belle and BaBar both define the ρ→ππ helicity angles in the cyclic convention, in which the ρ⁰ angle is referenced to the π⁻. They then extract α with the Lipkin–Nir–Quinn–Snyder relation A⁺⁺A⁻⁺²A⁰. That relation holds only if the ρ⁰ angle is referenced to the π⁺. The mismatch amounts to a sign flip of A⁰ and A̅⁰. Žlebčík corrects it by flipping the 12 of the 26 U/I parameters that are linear in A⁰ or A̅⁰, along with the corresponding covariance off-diagonals. He first reproduces the public HFLAV ρπ and combined curves exactly, then reruns the scan.

The corrected ρπ curve is much flatter near 90°. Its tension with the indirect value (91.2°) drops from 2.9σ to 2.1σ. The combined result becomes α=(87.0⁺¹¹.8_-4.7)^∘, compared with HFLAV’s (84.1⁺³.7_-3.0)^∘. The ππ+ρρ combination alone gives (85.9⁺⁸.6_-3.9)^∘.

The paper says every phenomenological treatment it examined carries the mismatch, including the Belle and BaBar papers, HFLAV/CKMfitter and UTfit. It traces the root cause to Snyder–Quinn never specifying the reference pion.

Caveats: - The apparent precision was partly an artefact. The combined upper error roughly triples, and ρπ no longer improves precision; only the 2σ interval tightens slightly, to [79.1°, 108.1°]. - The ρπ best-fit χ² rises from 8.4 to 9.5 (17 dof), although the combined χ² improves by 1.4. - A mirror solution near 0° persists.

For Belle II and LHCb, the practical lesson is that the Dalitz convention must be fixed before the isospin fit.

item.title: The LZ event with a two-state dark matter halo
item.dc:creator: Vinicius Oliveira
item.description:
Oliveira rebuilds LZ’s inference from public material. He uses a binned likelihood from the Fig. 5 projection (3 S1c slices × 32 bins), the shell-model nuclear response, and a toy-MC Neyman construction. The Helm form factor would overestimate the rate at 248 keV by a factor of 5, which is why the shell-model response matters. The recast matches LZ’s endothermic upper limits within 26% at all 17 points with δ ≥ 50 keV, and within 5% at about half of them. Its local significances run 0.2–0.7σ low: Z = 2.5 versus 3.0 at 1 TeV and δ = 300 keV.

The recast then allows a surviving excited-state fraction f. Freeze-out or freeze-in naturally gives f≈1/2 unless χ_2 decays. Exothermic scattering dominates above a critical f of 6×10⁻³, 1.4×10⁻³ and 3×10⁻⁵ at δ = 250, 300 and 350 keV. Above that point the required cross section scales as 1/f.

At f=1/2 and 1 TeV: - The best-fit σ_N drops by 80, 360 and 1.6×10⁴ at those three splittings. - σ_N stays within 3.5×10⁻⁴⁵–3.6×10⁻⁴⁴ cm² over 250–500 keV. - The endothermic cutoff disappears. - Di Mauro’s thermal benchmark (297 keV, 6.5×10⁻⁴³ cm²) sits 30× above the upper limit.

Caveats: - The exothermic intervals cannot be validated against any LZ result. - The likelihood is binned and the background is fixed. - Only the Standard Halo Model is used, which connects to Das et al. on halo dependence. - The paper does not impose the χ_2 lifetime bound. Radiative decay could drive f→0, which is exactly what Dutra et al. propose to test with a line in COSI. - The paper also flags unexplained internal inconsistencies in where LZ’s published lower limits turn on.

item.title: A First Glimpse at Super-Leading Logarithms in Monte Carlo Evolution
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Schalch
item.description:
Schalch extends the EFT-based Marzili framework to resum the SLL tower α_sⁿ⁺³L²ⁿ⁺³. The tower comes from two Glauber exchanges, arbitrarily many incoming-collinear emissions, and one terminal soft emission into the gap. The calculation is at the leading nonzero colour order, relative 1/N_c². The RG path-ordered exponential is turned into a shower-like sequence of Sudakov-sampled emissions acting on paired amplitude and conjugate-amplitude colour flows.

The key technical point is that retaining h=d+p≤2 bounds the flow mismatch to at most two partner swaps at any multiplicity. Glauber interference therefore survives without the colour space blowing up. In qq′, any real emission between the Glaubers gives zero. In qg, such emissions and unequal final flows contribute.

The validation is against analytic resummations at ΔY=2, ξ=α_sL²⁼⁸:

Channel Marzili Analytic
Octet (qq′) C_O=6.2759(47) 6.2754
Singlet (qq′) C_S=-11.6853(45) −11.6804
qg→qV C_qg=0.1099(247) 0.0971

The pronounced qg turnover is reproduced.

Caveats: - The calculation uses fixed coupling, strict-forward geometry and a single soft emission. The NGL–SLL interplay is not yet included. - There is a real sign problem in qg: the mean absolute weight is about 52× the mean signed weight, hence the ~25% error. - A mapping to CVolver’s cutoff-regulated Coulomb treatment is still open.

A parallel parton-shower effort (Helliwell) is noted.

The full texts of arXiv:2609.31833 and arXiv:2609.33151 were not supplied, so they are not expanded here.

item.title: Parnassus for the CLD Detector: A Generative Machine-Learning Surrogate for Detector Simulation and Reconstruction at the FCC-ee
item.dc:creator: Umar Sohail Qureshi et al.
item.description:
What they did. A two-stage conditional flow-matching model maps generator-level particles to CLD PandoraPFA objects:

  • Event stage: a residual MLP generates multiplicity, H_T and missing-momentum components.
  • Particle stage: a cross-attention DiT with about 5M parameters generates the objects themselves.
  • Outputs: kinematics, species, and d_0, z_0 with their significances.
  • Conditioning: the truth production vertex, which is what lets the model reproduce displaced heavy-flavor tails.

It was trained on Z→qq̅ and bb̅ at 91.2 GeV, with cc̅ and ss̅ held out as out-of-distribution tests.

Results.

  • Distance to full simulation: Parnassus is closer than Delphes for every observable, metric and flavor, typically by an order of magnitude. For example, W_1(d_0/σ_d_0) runs 0.14→0.41 from qq̅ to bb̅, against 2.06→4.94 for Delphes.
  • Tagging: a transformer tagger reproduces Pandora AUCs to within about 1%. For a tagger trained on full simulation and applied to surrogate jets, accuracy drops only from 0.694 to 0.682.
  • Speed: full simulation plus reconstruction costs 6.0 s per event. The surrogate costs about 39 ms per event on one CPU core and about 1.3 ms on an A100. The abstract quotes 1.2 ms.

Why it matters. Delphes’s CLD card overestimates flavor separability: it reaches 0.732 accuracy against Pandora’s 0.693. It also mis-models species fractions and m_jj. FCC-ee flavor-physics projections built on Delphes may therefore be optimistic. The authors frame this as their own caution about compensating effects in the transfer test.

Caveats.

  • Parnassus slightly underestimates separability. At 80% b-efficiency, the b-vs-c mistag is 1.58% against 1.00% for Pandora.
  • bb̅ is reproduced worse than the held-out cc̅ and ss̅ channels.
  • Validation covers only the Z pole.
  • Hyperparameters are taken unchanged from the CMS configuration.
  • The HitPF variant shows residual impact-parameter deviations.

item.title: Quantum probes of invisible particles in top-quark pair production at the LHC
item.dc:creator: Blanca Belmonte et al.
item.description:
What they did. This is a dileptonic tt̅+Y_0,1 study at 14 TeV and 3 ab⁻¹, with the invisible mediator at 10–100 GeV. The selection is E_T^miss>100 GeV and m_T2^ℓℓ>90 GeV. It reduces tt̅+tW to 0.04% while keeping 1.3% (scalar) and 4.0% (vector) of the signal at 10 GeV.

Four alternative analyses of the same sample are compared, and not combined:

  • the inclusive yield;
  • dN/dM^vis_tt̅;
  • dN/dD_evt;
  • the fiducial 𝒟(M^vis_tt̅), fitted with a Gaussian likelihood.

Results.

  • Exclusion ordering: yield < M^vis < D_evt < 𝒟(M^vis), for both mediator spins and all masses.
  • Robustness of the angular variable: D_evt with 50% shape uncertainty still beats M^vis with 20%.
  • Coupling structure: toy-calibrated scalar/pseudoscalar separation is also best with 𝒟(M^vis). The advantage grows at higher mediator mass, where rate-based discrimination degrades.

Why it matters. Spin information carries reach that rate and kinematics alone do not capture, which moves collider QI from demonstration to search tool.

Caveats.

  • The helicity frame is built from generator-level top momenta, which is truth-assisted.
  • E_T^miss is generator-level.
  • There is no detector simulation, and diboson and Z+jets backgrounds are neglected.
  • The gain rests on δ𝒟_syst=0.015 and is lost at about 0.05.
  • After cuts, 𝒟 is no longer a density-matrix quantity.
  • The axial-vector case is deferred because of unitarity issues.

item.title: Metastable Neutron Stars as Transient-Rate Detectors of Heavy Dark Matter
item.dc:creator: Ziwen Yin et al.
item.description:
What they did. For neutron stars in a metastable hadronic mass window, the present conversion rate is ℛ_tr=n_NSf_metaΓ_χe⁻Γ_χt_meta. This rate peaks at Γ_χ=1/t_meta. The benchmarks are:

  • n_NS=3×10¹⁵ Gpc⁻³;
  • f_meta=0.01;
  • t_meta=1 Gyr;
  • ℛ_SGRB=2×10³ Gpc⁻³yr⁻¹.

Requiring ℛ_tr below the SGRB rate excludes 7×10⁻¹¹<Γ_χ<4×10⁻⁹ yr⁻¹. An interval exists only if C<1/e; the benchmark gives C=0.067.

Resulting DM bounds. With U_max=10 GeV and gravitationally focused halo DM:

Channel Excluded band
Annihilation (m_χ≳5 GeV) 8×10⁻³⁴<⟨σv⟩(5 GeV/m_χ)²<5×10⁻³² cm³/s; disfavors thermal relics at 4×10³–3×10⁴ GeV
Decay 3×10²⁹<τ_χ(m_χ/10 GeV)<2×10³¹ s
Inelastic scattering σ_inel(10 GeV/m_χ) between 2×10⁻⁸⁰ and 10⁻⁷⁸ cm²
Macroscopic DM narrow band σ≈(1.3–1.6)×10⁻²⁷ cm² (with weak m_χ¹/19 scaling), for 4×10⁻⁷≲m_χ≲2×10¹⁴ g

Why it matters. The bound needs no individual star to be identified as hadronic. The allowed rapid-trigger branch has no analogue in survival-based bounds.

Caveats.

  • Every conversion is assumed to yield an observable SGRB, and all SGRBs are attributed to isolated sources (f_iso=1).
  • A single t_meta is used.
  • Energy is assumed to couple maximally to the nucleation mode (ϵ_bub∼1).
  • Only hadronic deposition counts; electromagnetic showers are too diffuse.
  • The local halo density of 0.4

item.title: Inclusive B decays, lifetimes, and |V_cb|: a unified heavy-quark expansion analysis
item.dc:creator: Matteo Fael et al.
item.description:
The default fit gives |V_cb|=(42.32±0.28_fit±0.10_h.o.)×10⁻³. Two methodological choices produce it. First, μ_α_s, μ_m_b^kin and μ_m_c are floated as fully correlated nuisances under a flat Rfit penalty. Second, no ad hoc power-correction covariance is added; missing orders are instead probed by refitting at 𝒪(1/m_b⁴,5). Across those orders |V_cb| moves by 0.2%, while μ_G² shifts by up to 43%.

The fit quality is poor: χ²/dof=119.5/67, p=8.4×10⁻⁵. Leave-one-out isolates the Belle q² moments, and dropping them gives p=0.23. The higher-order coefficients appear to absorb data tension rather than measure genuine power corrections. The fit also finds μ_G² about a factor 3 below the B^*–B splitting relation.

The central value is about 1σ above the recent 41.64±0.47, which includes 𝒪(α_em) effects that lower |V_cb|. For the digest’s inclusive-vs-exclusive tension, this is a tighter but method-dependent inclusive number. The authors caution that: - μ_α_s=9.13 GeV sits on the boundary of its range. - The reduced uncertainty “is inherent to the model” and not due to improved inputs. - With scales fixed, |V_cb|=43.18 with a ⁺¹.4_-0.7 scale variation.

Lifetimes come out 13% below experiment (1.1–1.2σ), rescued only by a strongly asymmetric non-leptonic scale error. The ratio τ_B⁺/τ_B⁰⁼¹.082⁺⁰.031_-0.013 agrees with 1.0832±0.0034. The actionable output is the call for new correlated moment and branching-fraction measurements.

item.title: Heavy Inert Doublet Reconciles LZ and IceCube
item.dc:creator: Hitoshi Murayama et al.
item.description:
Murayama and Noether reuse the Fan–Reece likelihood and find that the inert-doublet ϕ_0→ϕ_3 upscatter matches the higgsino phenomenology to 𝒪(10⁻⁹⁾. The LZ data fix the splitting, δ_0=368⁺¹²_-8 keV, essentially independently of mass; they do not select a mass. The 1/M number-density loss is offset by the halo integral as v_min falls.

The mass window comes entirely from other constraints: - Lower edge, 11.3 TeV: an independent re-implementation of the Bose et al. IceCube ν_μ solar limit (at σ_SI^loop=0) agrees with that analysis to 1–6%. - Upper edge, 20.3 TeV: freeze-out through longitudinal W/Z requires κ≈6.92 (M/11.3 TeV), which hits the unitarity bound κ<4π.

Expected yields are 0.05–0.72 events in the 215–270 keV window, compared with 0.93 for the 1.08 TeV higgsino.

The caveats are substantive: - Solar escape requires |η|≲0.013, but κ² running of η demands percent-level tuning of its initial condition. - The Landau pole sits at only ∼23M down to 6M, or 2.6M at large λ_Φ. - Neutrino spectra were generated at 1080 GeV and reused at all masses; the authors bound the resulting yield error to a factor 1.1–1.7.

ΔT≃0.0015 is harmless. The model is also untestable at FCC-hh.

item.title: Measuring Dual-Superconductor Length Scales in the QCD Vacuum at HERA
item.dc:creator: Tobias Toll et al.
item.description:
Toll and Vasim replace Gaussian hotspots with Clem’s vortex profile, K_0(√(b²⁺ξ_v²⁾/λ), in a Good–Walker dipole model. Coherent and incoherent moments are computed analytically, with log-normal saturation-scale fluctuations. They fit all 104 H1/ZEUS J/ψ photoproduction points (67 coherent, 37 incoherent; |t|<30 GeV², 40≤W≤251 GeV) and get χ²/ndf=70.8/98 at N_hs=8.

The extracted vacuum parameters are: - λ=0.191(5)(19) fm and ξ_v=0.087(5)(12) fm. - κ=2.7(3)(7), which is type-II. - 1/λ=1.03(11) GeV, compared with the lattice 1⁺⁻ gluelump at 0.87(15) GeV. The authors note that the gluelump value is scheme-dependent.

The Ginzburg–Landau string tension reproduces √(σ_0) for α_S=0.37(9), close to α_S(1/λ²⁾⁼⁰.36(2). Alternative tails (stretched exponential, power law) worsen the fit by Δχ²⁼³⁰. A floating tail exponent returns n=1.17(15), consistent with the K_0 value of 1.

Caveats: - The scalar sector fits less well. m_S=√(2)/ξ=3.9(7) GeV is 2.4(4)× the 0⁺⁺ glueball. - The dominant uncertainty comes from the weak sensitivity to N_hs. - A free normalization, about 1.2, is floated. - The type-II prediction of vortex repulsion cannot be tested, because saturation fluctuations are degenerate with geometric variance at |t|∼1 GeV². M_Y tagging at the EIC would break this degeneracy.

The claimed Q² independence is a clean EIC/LHeC test.

item.title: Hidden Region Finder
item.dc:creator: Einan Gardi
item.description: Neither the full text nor the abstract of this paper was supplied, so there is no deep dive. See the digest line for why it

item.title: Tension between MiniBooNE and MicroBooNE within a 3+1 Sterile Neutrino Framework using Simulation-Based Inference (Julia P. Woodward (Massachusetts Institute of Technology) et al.)
item.description:
With MiniBooNE’s f_π pion-flux correction removed, adding MicroBooNE BNB+NuMI data lowers the trials-calibrated 3+1 preference from ≥3.6σ (MiniBooNE alone) to 2.7σ. The two experiments sit in ≥2.5σ parameter-goodness-of-fit tension inside 3+1. The frequentist fit uses an SBI likelihood-ratio estimator (DNRE) with a normalizing-flow posterior (SNPE-C) to locate the best fit. The new ingredient is an SBI analogue of the Maltoni–Schwetz PG statistic, built from Δχ² differences relative to null. With it, 48,000 null trials become affordable.

The Wilks’ comparison shows why calibration matters. Without f_π, Wilks gives 7.1σ for MiniBooNE, 5.2σ for the joint fit, and 4.4σ tension. With f_π kept, the SBI joint preference drops to 1.8σ, but the tension rises to ≥3.2σ. In every f_π combination the BNB-only Wilks tension stays above 2σ, so the disagreement is not an artifact of inconsistent flux corrections.

Caveats: - Trial cap. 48k trials cap resolvable significance at ~4.25σ, so anything above 3.5σ is quoted as a lower bound. - Reconstructed NuMI prediction. MicroBooNE has released no event-level MC. The authors rebuilt the NuMI prediction from g4numi/PPFX/GENIE with a tuned approximate detector response (10-knot efficiencies per sample). Along the way they fixed a decay-at-rest flux bug worth up to 10% below 250 MeV. - Suspicious goodness of fit. MicroBooNE’s own χ²/dof of 86.62/179 is anomalously low. - Unexplained ν_μ excess. The low-energy ν_μ excess seen in both detectors is not understood, and the authors warn that quantitative comparisons should be read with care.

item.title: Sterile Neutrino Dark Matter Cries for GeV Heavy Neutral Leptons
item.dc:creator: Marco Drewes et al.
item.description:
This is the first νMSM scan using full quantum kinetic equations from baryogenesis through dark-matter production. The kinetics include chirality-flip effects, lepton-asymmetry back-reaction, and, decisively, the charge-odd (MSW-like) part of the HNL Hamiltonian. At the M₁ = 7 keV benchmark, the requirement to produce the QCD-epoch lepton asymmetry needed for Shi–Fuller conversion confines the HNL pair to a closed island.

Viable mass ranges: - Normal ordering (NO): the resonant-decay mechanism survives for 4 ≲ M ≲ 50 GeV. The 50 GeV upper bound is new. - Ignition mechanism (new): a self-amplifying MSW-driven instability that boosts μ_α by ~3 orders of magnitude, to |μ_α| ≃ 10⁻³. It reopens M < 5 GeV down to just above the kaon mass. - Inverted ordering (IO): only 0.8–7 GeV survives.

Experimental reach: - In the meson-accessible range, U² sits at least an order of magnitude above the seesaw floor. - SHiP covers the entire region below 2 GeV and much of 2–5 GeV. HL-LHC and Tera-Z machines cover the rest. - The predicted ΔM_phys adds a DM-specific test. For NO, HNL oscillation lengths can fall inside the SHiP decay volume; for IO, the pair looks Dirac-like.

Caveats: - A single DM mass is studied. - The scan uses momentum-averaged equations and neglects asymmetry depletion by N₁ production; both are checked only on the island boundaries. - Rates come from Fermi theory with free quarks, so the mass edges are uncertain below ~500 MeV and above ~50 GeV. - Structure-formation bounds on the computed spectra are deferred.

item.title: Big Bang Nucleosynthesis as a Probe of First-Order Phase Transitions
item.dc:creator: Masanori Tanaka
item.description:
Tanaka adds the reheating (α_n) dependence to BBN bounds on baryon inhomogeneity from supercooled transitions. The local reheating map is nonlinear, the spectral shape comes from the finite-bubble transition-time power spectrum, and proton/neutron diffusion is included. The result is imposed through the deuterium bound ε_BBN < 0.28 (1σ).

Results: - No bound exists for α_n < 0.1 with an optimistic k_cut = ∞, or for α_n < 0.5 with a conservative cut at the mean bubble separation. - For large α_n and 0.5 < T_n < 100 GeV, the disfavored region is β/H_n ≲ 5–6 (conservative) or ≲ 10–13 (optimistic). - Above ~10² GeV, diffusion weakens the bound.

NANOGrav: the NANOGrav-compatible region survives the conservative cut. It is largely disfavored only if the spectrum holds at sub-bubble scales, though much of it is still excluded keeping just modes with k < 2k_th. Evading the bound requires baryogenesis after reheating, or during the transition with baryon production tracking local entropy injection. That is the basis for the digest’s “baryogenesis timing” claim.

Caveats: - The result is 1σ only. - The baryon power spectrum is an admitted effective parametrization, and the bound is highly sensitive to the cutoff. - It assumes a pure exponential nucleation rate and energy release into the SM sector. - The paper is internally loose on bubble-wall baryogenesis. The abstract allows it if production tracks entropy, while Sec. 3 says the bound is “not evaded in general.” - A concurrent linearized analysis (Elahi et al.) finds β/H ≳ 10.3 α/(1+α), which Tanaka calls qualitatively consistent.

Full text was not supplied for the other two picks (Maier et al. arXiv:2609.26870, Gruzinov et al. arXiv:2609.26888), so no deep dives are given for them.

item.title: Discovery of an unexpectedly light and narrow beauty-strange state
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
LHCb reconstructs B_s⁰π⁰ candidates in 9 fb⁻¹ of Run 1–2 data across three B_s⁰ channels (D_s⁻π⁺, J/ψϕ, D_s⁻π⁺π⁺π⁻), finding a narrow peak at a common mass in all three. A simultaneous fit yields 343⁺⁴⁴_-41 signal events at M=5698.9±1.5±0.6 MeV/c², with local (global) significance exceeding 8 (7)σ. The width is consistent with zero, Γ<9.8 (11.8) MeV at 90% (95%) CL. Interpreted as the 0⁺ scalar B_s0^(5700)⁰ — the beauty counterpart of D_s0^(2317)⁺ — its B_s⁰ splitting of 332.0 MeV/c² tracks the charm-sector 349.2 MeV/c², and sits well below quark-potential predictions, the same “mass deficit” seen in charm. This is billed as the first observation of a nonconventional single-beauty hadron, extending the exotic-dynamics pattern (chiral doubling, BK molecules, or compact tetraquarks) into the open-beauty frontier that had lacked a counterpart.

The main caveat is spin-parity ambiguity: the structure is equally compatible with the 1⁺ axial-vector partner decaying to B_s^*0(→B_s⁰γ)π⁰ with the photon unreconstructed (then M=5748.3 MeV/c²), or a superposition of both. Resolving the (0⁺,1⁺⁾ doublet requires the B_s⁰γ spectrum and awaits the larger post-2022 upgrade dataset. The state also enables the first data-driven 0⁺ pole for B_s⁰ heavy-to-light form factors, and predicts light narrow partners for Ω_cc⁺ and broad B-sector states.

item.title: Observation of η(2600) and Threshold Enhancements in the ΛΛ̄ System
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
Using 2712.4 million ψ(3686) events, BESIII performs a model-independent partial-wave analysis of ψ(3686)→γΛΛ̅, exploiting the self-analyzing weak decays of Λ/Λ̅ to extract spin correlations and cleanly separate 0⁻⁺ from 0⁺⁺. The near-threshold region (97.6% purity) is dominated by the ¹S_0 (0⁻⁺, 13.2σ) and ³P_0 (0⁺⁺, 5.4σ) waves, both showing strong threshold enhancements. In the ¹S_0 wave a new pseudoscalar η(2600) emerges at M=2625±26±6 MeV/c², Γ=140±58±46 MeV, significance 7.0σ — mass-consistent with the X(2600) seen in J/ψ→γπ⁺π⁻η’, and the heaviest light meson to date. Its production relative to η_c (12–22%) matches the X(2600)/η_c ratio (31%) in the other channel, supporting a common identity. The ³P_0 wave gives a 2262±34 MeV/c², 215±35 MeV state near f_0(2200).

The finding supports theoretical suggestions of a pseudoscalar glueball-like state near 2.6 GeV, and the η(ΛΛ̅) threshold enhancement invites hexaquark/baryonium interpretations (a predicted pseudoscalar ΛΛ̅ bound state at ~2.27 GeV/c²). Caveats: the η(2600) mass and width depend on lineshape choice (BW vs K-matrix), the η(ΛΛ̅) pole position is model-unstable (BW mass 2169 vs KM 1899 MeV/c²), and the dominant systematic on the ³P_0 branching fraction reaches −22.8% from additional-wave assumptions.

item.title: Nonlocal advantage of quantum coherence in tau-lepton pairs from electron–positron collisions
item.dc:creator: Yoav Afik et al.
item.description:
Afik et al. argue that e⁺e⁻→τ⁺τ⁻ is uniquely suited to certify Nonlocal Advantage of Quantum Coherence (NAQC) — the strongest collider quantum correlation studied — because, unlike top pairs at the LHC where NAQC survives only in unmeasurably thin phase-space slivers, tau pairs exhibit NAQC over broad angular windows. For unpolarized T-states with symmetric correlation matrix, they show NAQC reduces to ∑_i|C_i|>√(6) and construct a single-observable witness W_NA=∑_i|C_ii| (maximized in the diagonal basis), measurable via a pion opening-angle distribution D_i=Tr[P_i𝐂]/3, with D_i≥√(2/3) sufficient for NAQC. At Belle II (√(s)=10.58 GeV) NAQC peaks at ℭ^l_1_NA,max=2.59 within |cosΘ|<0.23, containing f_NAQC=0.18 of events; at the FCC-ee Z pole, 2.96 within 0.39, f=0.31. A 5σ observation needs ~1% precision at Belle II, a few percent at FCC-ee.

The result matures the collider-QI program from entanglement toward a certifiable NAQC hierarchy (NAQC⊂Bell⊂…), and includes the first proposed steering-game implementation in a collider — with asymmetric steering flagged as a future CP-violation probe. Caveats are honest: event counts and NAQC signal are anti-correlated (both peak/dip at cosΘ=0); estimates omit detector acceptance and reconstruction efficiencies; and the analysis is LO electroweak with an ultrarelativistic T-state approximation. The general proof that NAQC implies Bell nonlocality remains missing (numerical evidence only).

item.title: First-Principles Determination of the QCD Contribution to the Axion-Photon Coupling Using Domain-Wall Fermions
item.dc:creator: Tian Lin et al.
item.description:
Using two near-physical N_f=2+1 domain-wall ensembles (24D and 32Dfine, both M_π≈143 MeV), Lin et al. compute 𝒞_QCD — the model-independent QCD piece of g_aγγ — via anomalous Ward identities rather than direct topological-charge insertion. The trick is to split 𝒞_QCD into an exact anomaly term (5/3-ξ, fixed by charge assignments and z=m_u/m_d) plus a light-quark-mass-suppressed correction extracted from the isoscalar P⁰-VV three-point function, itself only a few percent of the total. Continuum extrapolation gives 𝒞_QCD^IS=1.619(30), 𝒞_QCD^IB=0.347(22), and 𝒞_QCD=1.965(35), with the IB shift dominated by the explicit -ξ term and a tiny pion-pole correction (-0.0059, 0.3%).

Why it matters: this is an independent lattice benchmark for the quantity entering every axion-photon search, in a regime where E/N and 𝒞_QCD partially cancel. Crucially, the authors resolve the standing NLO ChPT spread (1.63–2.05): the SU(3) result had a sign error (since corrected by its authors), and the U(3) IB discrepancy traces to an effective m_u/m_d ~15% too large. With common inputs, ChPT and lattice reconcile. Caveat: chiral fermions keep discretization mild, but only two lattice spacings enter the continuum limit; the extrapolated correction carries ~60% statistical uncertainty, and systematics are explicitly “not yet complete.” Their IS value sits 2.2σ from the competing gluonic background-field determination (𝒞_QCD^IS=1.47(6)), underscoring the value of independent systematics.

item.title: Search for a top-philic heavy resonance in association with top quarks
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
ATLAS searches for a colour-singlet top-philic Z’ decaying to tt̅ and produced via tt̅ Z’ or tZ’, using same-sign-dilepton and ≥3-lepton final states in 140 fb⁻¹ (13 TeV) plus 56 fb⁻¹ (13.6 TeV). A mass-parameterised transformer classifier (Salt framework), fed event- and object-level features including the Z’ mass hypothesis, discriminates signal from the dominant tt̅ tt̅ and tt̅ W/Z/H backgrounds; tt̅ W and non-prompt backgrounds are constrained in dedicated control regions. No excess is seen (largest local significance 2.4σ at m_Z’=400 GeV, c_t=3). For c_t=1, θ=0, masses below 1150 GeV are excluded (1250 expected); for c_t=3, below 2000 GeV (θ=0). Cross-section limits improve ~15× over the previous ATLAS single-lepton tt̅ Z’ search, which could not exclude c_t=1 at any mass.

Why it matters: this is the vector-resonance handle the toponium-vs-scalar debate around the low-mass tt̅ excess has lacked — a direct top-philic Z’ constraint, now reaching c_t=1. The (c_t²,θ) scans exploit the interplay of three-top (tZ’, ∝cos²θ) and four-top (tt̅ Z’) modes. Caveats: the result is statistics-dominated, with leading systematics from tt̅ tt̅ modelling; the SM four-top cross-section itself sits high versus theory (22.5⁺⁶.6_-5.5 vs 12.0±2.4 fb), and an alternative +70% tt̅ tt̅ fit leaves the limit unchanged only through competing normalisation/uncertainty effects.

item.title: Interpreting the LZ 248 keV Event using Dark QCD
item.dc:creator: Francesco Sannino et al.
item.description:
Sannino and Turner read LZ’s 248±23_stat±23_sys keV recoil candidate as composite inelastic dark matter. A confining SU(3)_D theory with SM-singlet dark quarks produces a Dirac baryon B∼UUD; a dimension-ten, dark-number-violating operator involving a U(1)B-breaking scalar S splits it into two Majorana states χ_1,2 with δ=m_2-m_1. Endothermic χ_1 N→χ_2 N scattering, mediated by a leptophobic baryon-number vector V, suppresses low-energy recoils. Their benchmark — m_1=1 TeV, δ=300 keV, M_V=1.44 TeV, g_B=0.146 (M_V/g_B≃9.9 TeV) — gives σ_p⁰⁼⁶.5×10⁻⁴³ cm², inside LZ’s two-sided 90% interval, yielding ~0.26 accepted events in 2.84 tonne-years. A 300 keV splitting maps to a matching scale Λ*≃12 TeV for order-one coefficients. The construction embeds anomaly-cancelling spectators, a stabilising ℤ_18 (forbidding proton decay), and pion/pseudoscalar decay channels.

Why it matters: it is today’s cleanest confining-sector reading of the LZ event, tying the inelastic splitting to explicit dark-QCD dynamics rather than a bolted-on mass gap, and it survives solar-neutrino (σ_p⁰<9.9×10⁻⁴³ cm² for bb̅) and ATLAS dijet (g_q⁹⁵≃0.084>0.05) bounds. Caveats are frank: the benchmark probes the high-speed halo tail near threshold (E_R^⋆=267 keV), so rates depend sensitively on the assumed velocity distribution and nuclear response near a diffraction minimum; the event is only 2.6σ post-look-elsewhere; the excited fraction must be f_2<10⁻³; and relic abundance is treated as input, not derived.

item.title: Test of lepton flavor universality with B̅→D⁽*)τν̅_τ and B̅→D⁽*)ℓν̅_ℓ at Belle II
item.dc:creator: Belle II Collaboration et al.
item.description:
Using 387×10⁶ Υ(4S) decays with hadronic tagging, Belle II performs a simultaneous 2D fit in missing-mass-squared and residual calorimeter energy across five exclusive D⁽) samples, extracting R(D^)=0.242±0.019(stat)±0.016(syst) and R(D)=0.439±0.055±0.046 (correlations −0.40 stat, −0.20 syst). This supersedes the earlier hadronic-tag R(D^*) with twice the precision and delivers the first hadronic-tag R(D) at Belle II — the most precise hadronic-tagged determination to date, matching the best simultaneous measurements. Systematics are dominated by simulated-sample size (4.8%/8.4%) and, for R(D), B-tagging and low-momentum π⁰/γ efficiencies.

R(D^) sits within 0.5σ of the SM; R(D) is 2.0σ high, but the combination agrees with the SM at 1.5σ and with the world average at 1.3σ. The R(D^) central value landing below SM is the notable point for the LFU-anomaly narrative: this measurement neither sharpens nor kills the tension, easing rather than reinforcing it. Honest caveats are visible: the poorly-known gap-mode background is floated and found 42–82% smaller in data than simulation (validated against a B̅→D^π⁰ℓν control sample), and the hadronic-B normalization in the D^0_[D⁰π⁰] sample sits 3.1σ below prediction in the signal region — both absorbed into systematics rather than driving new uncertainty. The combined signal-plus-q²-sideband fit shifts the central values by only ~2%.

item.title: Observation of the doubly charmed baryon Ω_cc⁺
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
LHCb reports first observation of Ω_cc⁺ (scc) in Ω_c⁰π⁺, with Ω_c⁰→pK⁻K⁻π⁺, using 6.3 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV data from the upgraded detector. A BDT-driven selection (32% signal efficiency, background retention 2.4×10⁻⁴) yields a peak at 8.7σ global significance (9.0σ local; 184±24 signal events), validated against the Ξ_cc⁺⁺→Ξ_c⁺π⁺ control channel (2770±110 events). The mass is 3725.9±1.0(stat)±0.2(syst)±0.4(lifetime)±0.6(ext) MeV/c², extracted via the mass difference M(Ω_cc⁺⁾⁻M(Ξ_cc⁺⁺⁾⁼¹⁰⁴.3 MeV/c² to cancel momentum-scale and companion-pion biases. The structure persists above 9σ with a >170 fs decay-time cut, consistent with a weakly decaying state and disfavoring a strong resonance.

This completes the SU(4)_f spin-½ 20-plet of ground-state baryons — every predicted member now established — and lands squarely in the 3660–3780 MeV/c² theory window, adding another rung to the doubly-charmed spectrum after this year’s Ξ_cc⁺ observation. The main caveat is intrinsic: the Ω_cc⁺ lifetime is unmeasured, so the selection-induced mass bias (parameterized linearly over 90–190 fs, correction 0.30 MeV/c² at the 140 fs midpoint) carries a dedicated 0.4 MeV/c² uncertainty. Lifetime and additional decay channels await the larger Run 3 dataset already in hand.

item.title: LZ's Stairway to Heaνen: limits on elastic DM scatters from solar capture
item.dc:creator: Debajit Bose et al.
item.description:
Bose et al. take the elastic NREFT operators that LZ reported as ≥3σ fits to the 248 keV LZ230616 recoil and reverse-engineer their best-fit Wilson coefficients. Since LZ published favored regions only for ℒ_10^s (magnetic-dipole spin-spin) and the inelastic 𝒪_1^s, they build an approximate energy-dependent likelihood calibrated to reproduce LZ’s published local significances, validating against LZ’s own ℒ_10^s/𝒪_1^s curves (agreement to a factor of a few). They then compute solar capture rates (WimPyC) for each operator, assume equilibrium annihilation to {W⁺W⁻, bb̅, τ⁺τ⁻, νν̅}, and confront the resulting neutrino fluxes with IceCube (2016/2025 solar-direction ν_μ, 2014 atmospheric ν_e) and Super-K atmospheric data.

Large weak-scale mass ranges fitting LZ230616 are excluded, with the direct νν̅ channel giving the strongest and bb̅ the weakest limits; for ℒ_6^v, ℒ_8^s, ℒ_8^v the LZ-favored regions are almost entirely ruled out. This extends the “constraint-and-complementarity” mode the digest flags, mirroring the inelastic-operator treatment of Nguyen et al. Two honest caveats: the ℒ_4 operators survive even the νν̅ channel, and for several operators the excluded couplings lie where the EFT cutoff falls below the ~GeV solar-core momentum transfer — i.e., the NREFT description itself is invalid. Standard-halo velocities are assumed throughout, and LMC boosts or substructure could shift both the fits and the capture bounds.

item.title: Constraints on the Higgs boson total width from on-shell signal–background interference in H→γγ
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
ATLAS extracts a direct, coupling-independent bound on Γ_H from the interference between the resonant gg→H→γγ amplitude and the continuum diphoton background, which distorts the m_γγ lineshape — an antisymmetric peak shift (~-70 MeV at the SM width) plus a ~-1.7% yield reduction, both scaling as √(μ Γ_H/Γ_H^SM). Using the full 140 fb⁻¹ Run 2 dataset in two p_T^γγ categories, with m_H externally constrained from H→ZZ^*→4ℓ and μ profiled, they set an observed (expected) 95% CL limit Γ_H<307 (258) MeV, ~75× the SM value; the best fit is Γ̂H=13⁺⁷⁵-13 MeV and μ=1.08±0.12. Statistics-only, the limit tightens to 105 (87) MeV.

Why it matters: unlike the off-shell ZZ/WW method (ATLAS combined Γ_H=3.6⁺².1_-1.6 MeV), this probe makes no assumption that on- and off-shell couplings coincide, so it remains valid under exotic or invisible decays — a genuinely orthogonal handle even at ~30× weaker sensitivity. The caveat is explicit and dominant: the measurement is systematics-limited, with the largest single contribution (49 MeV at 68% CL) from the 39% theory uncertainty on the gg-interference K-factor (K_I=1.64, NLO→NNLOsv), followed by the m_H constraint (43 MeV). Because interference scales as √(Γ_H), the K_I uncertainty dominates entirely near the limit. The authors flag that interference calculations matched to parton showers are the needed improvement, and note only two p_T^γγ bins are justified given current modelling.

item.title: Computability of GPDs near x=±ξ in Lattice QCD
item.dc:creator: Yushan Su et al.
item.description:
Su, Ji, Liu, and Zhang argue that the LaMET large-momentum expansion for GPDs does not require the naive EFT condition 2|x±ξ|P^z≫Λ_QCD near the transition points x=±ξ, where one parton momentum vanishes. Their argument parallels DVCS factorization: soft contributions associated with the vanishing scale are power-suppressed, just as photon-DA physics enters DVCS only at O(Λ_QCD²/Q²⁾. The condition reduces to keeping at least one hard scale, 2(|x|+|ξ|)P^z≫Λ_QCD, dramatically enlarging the computable window that would otherwise exclude bands of width ~0.4 around x=±ξ for realistic P^z∼2–3 GeV.

Reanalyzing four existing nonzero-skewness datasets (ETMC20/21/25, MSULat23) with complete one-loop matching and a carefully ordered regulator hierarchy (ϵ_2≪|ϵ_1|→0, the only convergent ordering), they recover GPDs that are continuous at x=±ξ but with discontinuous derivatives — the expected partonic threshold kink from soft-quark zero modes, seen on the lattice for the first time and consistent with polynomiality-preserving GPD models. The previously reported discontinuities are attributed to regulator artifacts in the matching. This yields the first first-principles prediction of GPDs in the distribution-amplitude-like region (|x|<ξ), smoothly connecting quark and antiquark PDF-like regimes — directly relevant to DVCS extractions and the GUMP global-analysis program.

Caveats: the result rests on one-loop matching applied to existing data at coarse pion masses (mostly 260 MeV) and modest momenta, and the region remains uncomputable when both x and ξ are small (near x=0) or near the endpoints x=±1.

item.title: Observation of double ss̅ production in e⁺e⁻ collision at √(s)=3.08 GeV
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
BESIII reports the first systematic observation of double-ss̅ production in the e⁺e⁻ continuum, tagging a prompt ϕ recoiling against a second strangeness-carrying system X(ss̅) ∈{η,η’,K⁺K⁻,K⁺K^-,K⁻K^+,K⁰K̅⁰,K⁰K̅^0}. From 167 pb⁻¹, they measure σ(e⁺e⁻→ϕ+anything)=506.3±6.9±19.7 pb (a first) plus the individual ϕ+X(ss̅) cross sections, with ϕK⁺K^-, ϕK⁻K^+, ϕK⁰K̅⁰, ϕK⁰K̅^0 reported for the first time. After subtracting ISR (ϕγ_ISR) to isolate the QCD-driven part, the ratio is R_ss̅=(40.4±1.7_stat±1.5_syst)%.

Why it matters: this large ratio directly echoes the double-cc̅ surprise seen by Belle and BABAR at 10.6 GeV, where R_cc̅ exceeded early NRQCD predictions and drove years of theory refinement. Extending the phenomenon to the strange sector — in the deep non-perturbative regime — supplies a clean hadronization number that challenges the frameworks tuned to R_cc̅ and opens a window on possible flavor correlations in fragmentation. The synergy of strange and charm “flavor portals” is the framing.

Caveat, stated by the authors: the measurement omits higher-multiplicity final states (e.g. ϕK⁺K⁻π⁰), so R_ss̅ is a lower bound on total double-ss̅ rate; f_ss̅ assumptions for η/η’ and f-states carry model dependence, and several sub-channels have 6–11% systematics dominated by efficiency and background modelling.

item.title: Non-singlet splitting functions at four loops
item.dc:creator: Thomas Gehrmann et al.
item.description:
The full non-singlet splitting functions P_ns⁺, P_ns⁻, and P_ns^s=P_ns^v-P_ns⁻ are now known analytically at four loops for arbitrary Mellin moment n — the reference the field will cite for N³LO evolution. The method computes off-shell quark operator matrix elements for twist-two spin-n operators, using generating functions to keep n arbitrary while retaining standard IBP identities (via Qgraf, Form, Reduze2, and the finite-field Finred code). Rather than fight the elliptic geometries appearing in one color sector, the differential equations in the tracing parameter t are Taylor-expanded about t=0, where the integrals reduce to known four-loop propagator masters; moments up to n∼4000 are then generated and the all-n result reconstructed from an ansatz of harmonic sums up to weight 7. Results confirm all known color coefficients and reproduce independent fixed-moment checks, the four-loop cusp coefficient A_q⁽⁴⁾, and yield fully analytic virtual anomalous dimensions B_q⁽⁴⁾ and B_g⁽⁴⁾ plus the eikonal soft anomalous dimension f_r⁽⁴⁾.

Why it matters: consistent N³LO LHC cross sections require exactly these functions, previously available only as numerical approximations or partial analytics — anchoring today’s precision-QCD theme. Agreement with the Moch–Ruijl–Ueda–Vermaseren–Vogt numerics is good, though P_ns⁽³⁾,+ sits slightly above their error band at small x. One honest wrinkle: the ln⁴ x small-x terms disagree with the resummation prediction of Davies et al., by a piece subleading in N_c and proportional to ζ_2 — possibly an (iπ)² phase effect the authors flag for investigation. The singlet case remains, requiring gauge-variant operator renormalization.

item.title: Enhanced Standard Model bound on charm CP violation from QCD penguins
item.dc:creator: Ali Mohamed et al.
item.description:
Using light-cone sum rules with an auxiliary momentum inserted at the weak vertex (following the B→ππ methodology of Khodjamirian) to avoid parasitic cuts, Mohamed and Piscopo compute for the first time the QCD-penguin operator matrix elements for D⁰→K⁺K⁻ and D⁰→π⁺π⁻ at leading order in α_s. The scalar penguins Q_5,Q_6 are strongly enhanced: -i⟨Q_6⟩_ππ=2.09 GeV³ versus 0.228 for the current-current Q_1^d — roughly a factor of ten. Two sources drive this: quark-condensate contributions arising at tree level (enhanced by 16π² over the loop-induced terms) and an annihilation-type contribution from the u̅ u component entering already at twist three. Recomputed current-current matrix elements agree with the earlier Lenz et al. determination to within 5–10%, and the resulting branching ratios (ℬ(ππ)=1.22×10⁻³, ℬ(KK)=2.44×10⁻³) match HFLAV within their ~100% uncertainties.

Why it matters: the 2019 LHCb ΔA_CP∼10⁻³ needs penguin-to-tree ratios of order unity, an order of magnitude above naive estimates, and whether this fits the SM hinges on hadronic matrix elements. Enhanced penguins narrow the SM-vs-experiment gap — direct progress on the standing charm-CPV puzzle flagged in August. Caveat, stated plainly: the strong phases remain unconstrained at LO α_s, so no quantitative CP-asymmetry prediction follows; the bound assumes maximal phases. The annihilation approximation carries an expected ≥30% error because s_0/m_D²∼20–30% (versus ~3% for B decays).

item.title: Dark Radiation Sticks Together: Dark QCD and the Hubble Tension
item.dc:creator: Matthew R. Buckley et al.
item.description:
Buckley, Fernandez, and Putney propose a confining SU(N_c) dark sector with heavy stable quarks (the dark matter) and light quarks whose confinement at Λ_D∼ MeV turns the dark radiation into light dark pions. Crucially, residual strong interactions make this radiation a viscous imperfect fluid rather than free-streaming — modeled in a modified CLASS with drag (Γ_drag) and relaxation-time equations. The viscosity suppresses high-ℓ CMB oscillations relative to free-streaming ΔN_eff, letting the model raise H_0 without spoiling the high-ℓ multipoles or S_8. A full MCMC over Planck, ACT, DESI DR2, Pantheon+, SH0ES, and BBN yields H_0=71.60±0.63 km/s/Mpc with a residual tension of ∼3σ (Q_DMAP=3.0σ vs 6.0σ for ΛCDM), competitive with Hubble World Cup “finalists.” It also fits DESI BAO better than Planck-only ΛCDM.

Why it matters: this is a genuinely different mechanism for the Hubble tension — not just extra N_eff, but self-interacting radiation whose fluid behavior evades the high-ℓ constraints that cap free-streaming models near 4σ. The large late-time self-interaction cross section (∼Λ_D⁻²) evades Bullet Cluster bounds because hard momentum transfer requires perturbative heavy-quark scattering. Honest caveats: the best-fit Λ_D∼1 MeV produces dark acoustic oscillations in tension with Lyman-α, though Λ_D≳3–5 MeV evades this with negligible fit degradation; and the CLASS modifications were partly LLM-generated.

item.title: Confronting the Higgsino Interpretation of the LZ Event with Astrophysical Uncertainties and Solar Capture
item.dc:creator: Aditya Ghosh et al.
item.description:
The higgsino reading of LZ’s 248 keV recoil cannot survive the solar-capture bound no matter how the halo is stretched. Ghosh, Chavez, and Kelso compute the expected LZ signal for a 1.1 TeV thermal higgsino (WimPyDD, including the factor-4 cross-section correction of Pospelov–Ramani) across the full Standard Halo Model parameter space and, separately, using N-body hydrodynamical halos that include the LMC’s imprint on the high-speed tail. IceCube/Super-K non-observation of solar annihilation neutrinos requires the inelastic splitting δ≳506–566 keV, which for a 248 keV xenon recoil demands lab-frame speeds v_min∼950–1025 km/s. In the SHM, the δ≳566 keV bound requires v_0≳240 km/s independent of v_esc — well beyond the 2σ range of any measured v_0 (up to 256 km/s), even at optimistic ρ_χ=0.45 GeV cm⁻³ and with a 5%-probability upward fluctuation. In the LMC-aware simulated halo, δ=514 keV is the largest splitting that yields one event in the 200–300 keV window; all curves fall below the fluctuation threshold by δ∼530 keV.

Why it matters: This is exactly the discriminator mode the digest tracks — an attempt to close the last astrophysical escape hatch rather than add another fit. The thermal higgsino is now doubly cornered: kinematics and solar capture together leave no viable window at δ≳566 keV.

Caveat: Only the weaker δ≳506 keV bound (tree-level Z up-scatter, not the loop-induced elastic channel) leaves a sliver of SHM viability, and only when both v_0 and v_esc sit at their upper limits. The LMC-tail extension beyond 950 km/s is a phenomenological exponential, not a simulated result.

item.title: Argon as the test of two interpretations of the LZ 248 keV recoil
item.dc:creator: Howard Baer et al.
item.description:
Baer and Barger reduce the endothermic-vs-exothermic debate to a single already-recorded measurement. Both interpretations require an internal splitting, but they flow energy oppositely. Read exothermically (pseudo-Dirac downscatter releasing |δ|), the event predicts a nuclear-recoil line in argon at E_Ar=|δ| m_χ/(m_χ+m_Ar) — 336 keV for m_χ=200 GeV, ranging 268–525 keV over the exothermic family — at ~3–4 events/tonne-yr, roughly ten times the equivalent xenon rate. Argon wins because its Helm form factor at 336 keV sits in the first diffraction lobe (F²⁼⁰.056) while xenon at 248 keV sits near its second-lobe minimum (F²⁼¹.6×10⁻⁴); the factorized rate ratio returns 9.5 at 200 GeV. Read endothermically (ground-state upscatter by the fast halo tail), argon predicts zero events: the argon threshold speed exceeds the halo maximum (1224 vs 796 km/s at 1.1 TeV). The ratio depends only on two-body kinematics, the two form factors, and the coupling’s charge structure — not the mediator or excited fraction.

Why it matters: DEAP-3600 already holds the data. The published 231-day exposure implies ~7 events (full target) or 1.7 (fiducial) at the benchmark rate; the 813-day first run holds ~25 and 6. A reanalysis for single-scatter nuclear recoils between 200–600 keV (near 85 keV_ee) either finds the line and fixes m_χ from the two line positions, or kills the exothermic reading — no new detector required.

Caveat: The fiducial mass at ~500 photoelectrons is unpublished; expected counts within the WIMP-search fiducial volume are only a few, and background control (shadowed alphas, ³⁹Ar, radiogenic neutrons) rests on DEAP’s own estimates.

item.title: First Observation of D_s⁺→f_0(980)μ⁺ν_μ
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
BESIII observes the semi-muonic decay D_s⁺→f_0(980)μ⁺ν_μ (with f_0→π⁺π⁻) for the first time, using 7.33 fb⁻¹ at E_CM=4.128–4.226 GeV and a double-tag technique (839k single tags across 15 hadronic modes). From 196±22 signal events they measure ℬ=(1.59±0.18_stat±0.11_syst)×10⁻³. Combined with the earlier BESIII electronic-channel result, the LFU ratio ℬ(μ)/ℬ(e)=0.92±0.13_stat±0.08_syst agrees with the SM range 0.94–1.11 — no LFU violation at current precision, and the first such test in a scalar-meson c→s transition. A dynamical fit (simple-pole form factor, relativistic Flatté line shape) yields f_+^f_0(0)|V_cs|=0.490±0.059±0.025; averaging with the electronic channel gives 0.500±0.016±0.020, and with CKMfitter |V_cs| the most precise D_s→f_0 form factor to date, f_+^f_0(0)=0.514±0.017±0.021.

Why it matters: Beyond extending LFU tests into scalar final states, the branching fraction implies a mixing angle ϕ=(28.0±26.6)^∘, favoring an ss̅-dominant f_0(980) in the qq̅ picture. The precise form factor discriminates sharply among models: consistent with CLFD/DR/QCDSR but in up-to-5σ tension with LCSR, LFQM, and CCQM predictions, all of which now incorporate the finite f_0 width. This is the consolidating-null flavor picture the digest notes — LFU intact, precision turned onto hadronic structure.

Caveat: The 13% statistical LFU uncertainty leaves ample room; the extracted ϕ carries a large error. μ/π misidentification is handled by retaining both track pairings and fitting the wrong-combination shape.

item.title: What has the LHC told us about the electroweakino sector of the MSSM?
item.dc:creator: Peter Athron et al.
item.description:
GAMBIT’s most complete collider recast of the MSSM electroweak sector to date: a frequentist global fit over 34 Run 2 LHC searches, 63 Run 2 measurements (via Contur), and LEP cross-section limits, scanning M_1, M_2, μ, tanβ with all other sparticles decoupled. The headline is that a genuine general bound now exists where the 2018 fit found none — for a light bino χ̃_1⁰, exclusion reaches m_χ̃_2⁰≳760 GeV in both the (m_χ̃_2⁰,m_χ̃_1⁰⁾ and chargino planes. Adding a light (m_3/2=1 eV) gravitino pushes exclusions to (m_χ̃_1⁰,m_χ̃_2⁰⁾∼(900,1000) GeV, but a Higgsino-dominated LSP survives down to ≈650 GeV. The much-discussed ATLAS soft-dilepton excess (Δm∼20 GeV) is reproduced as a weak preference near m_χ̃_2⁰≈200 GeV, but the CMS zero-lepton and soft-lepton searches disfavour exactly the ATLAS-preferred region — no scenario fits both simultaneously.

Why it matters: this is the empirical backdrop the month of LZ-higgsino fits has largely ignored. The Higgsino-degenerate corner that survives at ~650 GeV is precisely where compressed dark-matter scenarios live, and closing it at small Δm is conceded to be “very challenging” even at HL-LHC. Honest caveats: signal yields use LO+LL (not NLO) cross-sections, monojet and long-lived-particle searches are omitted, the b-jet regions of ATLAS_2BoostedBosons are not implemented, and the G̃-EWMSSM best fit rests on a 36 fb⁻¹ CMS diphoton excess that newer full-Run-2 photon searches do not corroborate.

item.title: Search for a light pseudoscalar Higgs boson in boosted μμττ final states
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
CMS searches H→aa→μμττ in 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV data, where the large m_H–m_a hierarchy collimates each ττ pair. The key methodological advance is dedicated boosted-ditau reconstruction: modified HPS seeding for τ_μτ_h/τ_eτ_h (efficiency gains up to factors of 2–4 at high m_H), plus a new deep-network tagger, DeepDiTau, that classifies AK4 jets as τ_hτ_h at 70% efficiency and ~1% mistag — enabling the high-rate all-hadronic channel for the first time. Combining four ττ channels covers 94% of a→ττ decays. No excess is seen. Model-independent 95% CL limits on σ_H×ℬ/σ_SM reach 5×10⁻⁵ to 2.7×10⁻⁴ for m_a=3.6–21 GeV at m_H=125 GeV, and — for the first time at the LHC in ττ final states — extend to a heavy scalar up to m_H=1 TeV, where limits span 3.5×10⁻⁴ to 1.5×10⁻³ for m_a=3.6–50 GeV.

Why it matters: this is the day’s genuine light-pseudoscalar collider result, complementary to the LZ/axion model-building. It sets the most stringent ℬ(H→aa) limits to date for 3.6<m_a<4.2 GeV in Type-I/II 2HDM+S, improves on prior μμττ results by factors 2–5, and opens the heavy-scalar →aa window entirely. Caveats: sensitivity degrades at low m_a where decay products fully merge, Υ resonances contaminate near m_a≈10 GeV, and above 4.2 GeV the charm-tagging analysis remains stronger.

item.title: Constraints on Galactic Dark Photons from a DALI Prototype
item.dc:creator: Javier De Miguel et al.
item.description:
A proof-of-principle DALI haloscope — a 20-plate yttria-stabilized zirconia Fabry–Pérot resonator read out by an antenna, run at fixed λ/8 spacing with Q_L≈2200 near 6.907 GHz and T_sys≃59 K — reinterprets 36 hours of data (originally an axion search) as a dark-photon search. No magnetic field is needed since kinetic mixing converts dark photons at the dielectric discontinuities. After baseline removal, iterative RFI masking, grand-spectrum stacking with the lab-frame line shape, and an end-to-end injection efficiency of η_e2e≃0.60, no significant excess survives. Fourteen retained clusters all fall below adopted confidence and are flagged for rescan. The result excludes kinetic mixing χ≲6.8×10⁻¹⁴ at 28.54 μeV (6.902 GHz), across 88.1% of the unmasked 28.482–28.610 μeV band at 90% CL — claimed as the strongest laboratory bound in this frequency range.

Why it matters: it fits today’s haloscope theme (alongside DALI’s companion resonator paper), demonstrating that the open Fabry–Pérot architecture — whose cross section decouples from resonance frequency — can deliver competitive high-frequency limits with mature commercial hardware. As a magnet-free dark-photon channel, it is a cheap, fast complement to cavity haloscopes. Caveats are explicit: only a single frequency step (one plate spacing), a scaled-down prototype (~1:100 in area), an undercoupled antenna (β≃0.36), assumption that dark photons saturate the local density with randomly-oriented polarization (κ²⁼¹/3), and a residual 0.09σ baseline systematic.

item.title: Qubit-Qutrit Quantum Tomography of hadronic Λφ and ΛK*⁰ systems
item.dc:creator: Veronica Kanachova et al.
item.description:
Extending collider quantum tomography to unequal-spin final states, Kanachova et al. formalize the spin-½⊗1 density matrix for Λφ and ΛK*⁰ pairs and confront its inescapable incompleteness: the parity-violating Λ→pπ⁻ is fully self-analyzing, but the parity-conserving V→PP decay carries no rank-1 (dipole) analyzer, so only 23 of the 35 spin parameters are measurable — the meson vector polarization Pᵢ (3) and the dipole–dipole correlations Cᵢⱼ (9) drop out identically. The key result is that entanglement can still be certified exactly from this censored data. Zeroing the 12 missing parameters is equivalent to a “partial time reversal” on the meson (𝒰_B∘T_B), and the reconstruction ρ_meas satisfies ρ_meas^{T_B}=𝒰_B(ρ_meas), so the Peres–Horodecki test collapses to a single diagonalization: a negative eigenvalue of ρ_meas certifies entanglement, with no false positives, and no analysis of the same 23 observables can do better. Pure entangled states retain exactly half their negativity; mixed states have quantifiable “blind windows” (e.g. isotropic-noise dilution entangled for p>1/4 but uncertifiable until p>2/5).

Why it matters: this opens a new hadronization probe. Because local dressing cannot create entanglement, surviving correlations lower-bound the quark-pair correlation at production, and comparing degradation in Λφ/ΛK*⁰ (meson channel) against ΛΛ̄ (baryon channel) as a function of ΔR isolates p_meson vs p_baryon — a coherence-transport quantity never measured. Estimators are simple angular moments extractable from existing datasets. Caveat: the theorems’ validity relies on the specific 12-parameter censoring; other 12-subsets give false positives, and much of the numerical verification was AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5) with a stated but unproven pure-state conjecture.

item.title: Positive- and negative-parity charm-strange and bottom-strange mesons from lattice QCD
item.dc:creator: Forrest Guyton et al.
item.description:
Guyton and Meinel deliver a full RBC/UKQCD determination of decay constants, binding energies, and Weinberg compositeness for the lightest scalar, pseudoscalar, vector, and axial-vector Dₛ and Bₛ mesons, using domain-wall light/strange quarks and anisotropic clover charm/bottom on seven ensembles (mπ = 139–431 MeV, a = 0.073–0.114 fm) with combined chiral-continuum extrapolation. For negative-parity states they obtain f_{Dₛ}=251.4(2.1)(0.4)(2.5) MeV, f_{Dₛ}=272.5(4.3)(1.0)(2.7), f_{Bₛ}=228.4(5.8)(0.5)(2.3), f_{Bₛ}=229.2(4.4)(0.8)(2.3) MeV, plus ratios f_{Dₛ}/f_{Dₛ}=1.086(14)(11) and f_{Bₛ}/f_{Bₛ}=1.003(22)(10), consistent with FLAG. The positive-parity sector uses a GEVP with q̄q, derivative, and meson-meson-scattering operators (the latter at both source and sink), Lüscher’s method, and effective-range expansions to extract infinite-volume bound-state masses: m_{Dₛ0}−m_D−m_K=−48(14)(4) MeV, m_{Dₛ1}−m_{D}−m_K=−61(15)(2), m_{Bₛ0}−m_B−m_K=−69(13)(4), m_{Bₛ1}−m_{B}−m_K=−77(10)(5). The charm results agree with experiment (−45.0(6), −44.7(6) MeV). Positive-parity decay constants — including the first-ever lattice f_{Bₛ0*}=207(12)(8)(2) and f_{Bₛ1}=196(16)(11)(2) MeV — are reported.

Why it matters: the below-threshold binding, small positive-parity decay constants, and scattering lengths consistently support a predominantly D⁽⁾K/B⁽⁾K molecular interpretation of the Dₛ0*(2317)-like states, and the negative-parity constants feed dispersive bounds on b→s form factors relevant to the b→sℓℓ anomalies. Caveats acknowledged: two-pion left-hand cuts (which extend above the ground-state energies at low mπ) are neglected, invalidating strict Lüscher/ERE there, and weak-binding corrections to Weinberg’s criterion are expected to be large in some channels.

item.title: Distinguishing a pseudoscalar from a vector t t̄ resonance with top-quark spin correlations at the HL-LHC
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Bellagroudi et al.
item.description:
Bellagroudi and Fassi ask a post-discovery question: given a t t̄ resonance, can dilepton spin correlations separate a CP-odd 2HDM pseudoscalar A (0⁻, spin-singlet ¹S₀, iγ₅ vertex) from a leptophobic topcolor Z′ (1⁻, chiral vector)? Using MadGraph+Pythia+Delphes with matrix-element spin-preserving decays and neutrino-weighting reconstruction, they find a parton-level helicity-correlation gap Δc_hel≃0.43 (A: +0.33, Z′: −0.08), nearly mass-independent, surviving reconstruction with dilution ≈0.66. Normalizing A to CMS HIG-22-013 coupling limits and rate-matching Z′ so the test probes spin structure, the LO t t̄-only baseline gives 2.27σ (400 GeV) and 2.74σ (800 GeV) at 3000 fb⁻¹, using a 4×4 (c_hel, c_han) template likelihood. Reverse non-nested direction agrees; equal-yield tests give 1.86 and 2.70σ (confirming 800 GeV is shape-driven); profiling a Gaussian-constrained SM c_hel nuisance yields 2.07/2.63σ (optimistic) down to 1.67/2.26σ. A g⁴-mapped scan places 5σ at couplings ~22%/16% above reference.

Why it matters: this makes the toponium-vs-scalar interpretation debate quantitative, showing spin correlations can in principle assign resonance spin/parity where a rate excess cannot. The 800 GeV point is the cleanest demonstration; 400 GeV is intrinsically fragile because the near-threshold SM continuum is itself spin-singlet/pseudoscalar-like (the same physics driving threshold entanglement enhancement), and 1500 GeV is unreachable (~12 events). Honest caveats abound: LO normalization, fixed on-shell widths, no non-t t̄ backgrounds, and — critically — omitted signal–continuum interference, plus a single-mode “bracket” nuisance rather than a proper mass-dependent sideband fit.

item.title: Heavy Higgsino Interpretation of the LZ Event
item.dc:creator: Kevin Langhoff
item.description:
Langhoff performs a 2D likelihood fit of pure-higgsino inelastic scattering to the LZ 248 keV recoil plus the empty high-energy sideband (350–675 keV), then folds in recomputed IceCube solar-capture bounds. The data alone prefer a light branch, m_χ≈(240,450) GeV, but that region is excluded by solar capture (which sets a floor on the splitting δ via neutrinos from captured-higgsino annihilation). The thermal higgsino at 1.1 TeV overfills the sideband (N_SB≳2, Δχ² up to 11). The only corner consistent with the event, the empty sideband and solar capture is m_χ≈(10⁵,10⁶⁾ GeV with δ≈(330,480) keV — where DM dilution (ρ∝1/m_χ) forces small δ and the sideband/ROI event ratio lands near 0.8–1 (versus ∼0.1 light, ≳15 thermal), a testable prediction. Such a heavy higgsino cannot arise from freeze-out, so he builds a proof-of-concept: freeze-out during early matter domination reheating to T_RH≈1 TeV, tied to the μ term via a Kim-Nilles mechanism that also solves strong CP.

Why it matters: it closes today’s headline arc — the ordinary thermal reading is dead, and survival demands a 10⁷ GeV gaugino scale plus a bespoke cosmology, connecting a direct-detection anomaly to axion/strong-CP physics. Caveats are frank: the Δχ² contours are a “heuristic guide” only, the heavy point is not the best fit, results depend on LMC-tail halo modeling, solar-capture curves bracket limiting behavior rather than a precise bound, and the model needs a tuned axion misalignment (θ≲0.05).

item.title: Nucleon Strong-Interaction Size from Charmonium Photoproduction
item.dc:creator: Xiangdong Ji et al.
item.description:
Ji, Joosten, Meziani, and Pefkou extract the nucleon’s overall strong-interaction radius by combining world near-threshold J/ψ photoproduction data (GlueX, Hall C, CLAS12) with a recent Bayesian quark-sector GFF analysis. Fitting the differential cross sections in a holographic-QCD model — A_g(t) dipole, C_g(t) tripole, B_g=0 — yields the gluon stress-energy form factors (χ²/ndf=1.005 after dropping the lowest GlueX energy bin). Energy-momentum conservation then relates the total A,C form factors to the scalar (trace-anomaly) color-field distribution G^s(t), whose Breit-frame radius is ⟨r_s²⟩¹/2=0.94±0.09 fm — larger than the PDG charge radius (0.8409 fm) and larger than the mass radius, defining a gluonic “skin” analogous to the neutron skin in ²⁰⁸Pb.

Why it matters: it delivers a clean, quotable first experimental number for the nucleon’s strong-interaction extent, mapping the color field that generates most of the nucleon mass rather than its charge. The ordering (strong > charge > mass) agrees with lattice and dispersive determinations cited. Caveats are stated plainly: the identification of the photoproduction amplitude with the gluonic SET is framework-dependent (open-charm and alternative production mechanisms may contaminate), B_g=0 is an assumption, and the result inherits both statistical and model uncertainty. SoLID and EIC/ePIC are projected to improve precision by up to an order of magnitude.

item.title: Can Elastic Neutrino Scattering Account for the LZ230616 Event?
item.dc:creator: Ayan Chattaraj et al.
item.description:
Chattaraj et al. systematically test whether coherent elastic neutrino–nucleus scattering (CEνNS) can produce the 248 keV LZ recoil. Kinematics alone require E_ν≳118 MeV, killing solar and DSNB fluxes; only atmospheric neutrinos reach that energy, but their SM rate in the signal bin (225–271 keV) is R_I≃2×10⁻⁶ events. Introducing BSM scalar or vector mediators tuned to give one signal-region event overshoots the low-energy bins by 𝒪(10⁵⁾ events — six orders of magnitude above background — so the R_I=1 contour sits entirely inside the R_II-excluded region. Exotic monochromatic fluxes fare no better: DM annihilation (χχ→νν̅) requires ⟨σv⟩≳10⁻¹⁸ cm³/s and DM decay τ_χ≲10¹⁵ s, both far past existing bounds, while overpopulating low-recoil bins by hundreds of events. PBH evaporation is worst: the exponentially soft Hawking spectrum gives R_II/R_I∼10⁴–10²³ and demands f_PBH≳95, exceeding the total DM density.

Why it matters: the useful null of the day. The broad recoil spectrum inherent to elastic scattering is fundamentally incompatible with an isolated high-energy feature, reinforcing that the LZ event demands an inelastic/threshold mechanism (higgsino, exothermic DM). Caveat: the analysis is deliberately restricted to elastic channels — inelastic neutrino processes and atmospheric-neutrino upscattering (their ref. [29]) are outside scope.

item.title: From LUX-ZEPLIN to Colliders: Probing Higgsino Dark Matter
item.dc:creator: Kingman Cheung et al.
item.description:
Taking the 248 keV LZ recoil at face value as 1.1 TeV thermal Higgsino inelastic DM with neutral splitting δm_0≃350 keV, Cheung, Kang, and Kumar work out the necessary collider corollary: the charged Higgsino sits Δm_+∼(330–350) MeV above the neutral state (electroweak loops dominating over a ∼-9 MeV finite-gaugino tree contribution), giving proper lifetime τ≈0.025 ns, cτ≃(6–8) mm, and decays to a soft ∼300 MeV pion. This is a sub-centimeter disappearing tracklet. Current ATLAS disappearing-track (m_χ^±≲225 GeV) and CMS soft-track (≲185 GeV) limits sit far below the 1.1 TeV target because the survival probability through three pixel hits (R∼9 cm) is ∼3×10⁻⁶ at β_Tγ=1; the 0.57 fb production cross section compounds the problem. HL-LHC needs better short-track reconstruction, not luminosity; dedicated studies find 5σ reach at a 100 TeV collider (30 ab⁻¹) and a 10 TeV muon collider (10 ab⁻¹).
